# Dine Doubles Down on Dual-Brand IHOP-Applebee’s Growth as Consumer Spending Softens

 Aug  17  2026 

 Feature 

![Image 25: Applebee's-IHOP restaurant.](https://www.fsrmagazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/applebeesihop.jpg)

 Dine Brands 

 The first U.S.-based Applebee's-IHOP store opened in early 2025. 

Share:

[Tweet](https://twitter.com/share?url=https://www.fsrmagazine.com/feature/dine-doubles-down-on-dual-brand-ihop-applebees-growth-as-consumer-spending-softens/&text=Dine%C2%A0Doubles%20Down%20on%20Dual-Brand%20IHOP-Applebee%E2%80%99s%20Growth%20as%20Consumer%20Spending%20Softens%C2%A0 "Share on Twitter")[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.fsrmagazine.com/feature/dine-doubles-down-on-dual-brand-ihop-applebees-growth-as-consumer-spending-softens/&display=popup&ref=plugin&src=share_button "Share on Facebook")[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https://www.fsrmagazine.com/feature/dine-doubles-down-on-dual-brand-ihop-applebees-growth-as-consumer-spending-softens/ "Share on LinkedIn")[Email](mailto:?subject=Your%20friend%20has%20shared%20an%20article%20with%20you.&body=Dine%C2%A0Doubles%20Down%20on%20Dual-Brand%20IHOP-Applebee%E2%80%99s%20Growth%20as%20Consumer%20Spending%20Softens%C2%A0%0D%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fwww.fsrmagazine.com%2Ffeature%2Fdine-doubles-down-on-dual-brand-ihop-applebees-growth-as-consumer-spending-softens%2F%0D%0A "Share via Email")

The Applebee’s and IHOP parent is using its value-led “barbell” strategy, restaurant remodels, and dual-brand conversions to counter a more selective consumer. 

After breaking its sales slump and posting its first portfolio-wide flat-to-positive sales performance in years [last quarter](https://www.fsrmagazine.com/feature/dine-brands-breaks-sales-slump-hitting-first-portfolio-wide-sales-gain-in-years/), Dine Brands entered the second quarter of 2026 with a slightly less glamorous story.Same-store sales fell 1.8 percent year-over-year at Applebee’s, for example, despite raising menu prices.

But Dine aims to look past short-term quarterly gains and losses and focus heavily on its biggest long-term bet: dual-branded Applebee’s-IHOP stores.

The dual-brand format uses one shared entrance, with Applebee’s and IHOP each represented in separate seating zones—red for Applebee’s and blue for IHOP. Guests choose either side and order from one streamlined menu organized by daypart, featuring the strongest items from both brands and a few dual-brand exclusives.

After seeing success with the first U.S. dual-brand in Seguin, Texas, where sales nearly tripled compared to the previous IHOP, Dine began expanding the format aggressively. The company is targeting 80 dual-brand restaurants by year-end, nearly doubling its current footprint of 45 open locations, including seven company-owned stores and 12 additional under construction. And it’s not a short-term strategy; Dine Brands CEO John Peyton [projects room for 900 dual-branded units](https://www.fsrmagazine.com/feature/dine-brands-sees-room-for-900-applebees-ihop-combo-restaurants/) over the next decade.

The first Los Angeles dual-brand store, Peyton noted, is already performing well. “Opened by an existing franchisee who knows our brands well, the location is already performing at high sales levels,” he said—“a strong proof point that the concept can win in new markets and that experienced operators are continuing to lean in.”

Franchisee interest in the dual-brand program continues growing, since converting a single-brand location into a dual-branded restaurant can roughly double its revenue, Peyton said. Conversion costs average about $1 million. The company expects the added sales and profit contribution to justify the investment over time, especially as it learns how to optimize labor, kitchen operations, and daypart mix across both concepts.

However, that investment is contributing to near-term financial pressure. Dine’s second-quarter revenue rose 4.4 percent to $240.9 million, aided by its growing company-owned restaurant portfolio, but adjusted EBITDA declined 3.6 percent to $54.2 million. Adjusted diluted earnings per share were essentially flat at $1.16.

The company also ended the quarter with 136 company-owned restaurants, including locations acquired from franchisees. Dine’s plan is to remodel those units, stabilize performance, and refranchise them over the next three years.

As far as single concepts go, Applebee’s had a relatively more difficult last few months than its sister brands, with traffic down as menu pricing rose 3.4 percent this quarter. Peyton attributed the chain’s 1.8 percent comp sales decline,in part, to inflation in food away from home, elevated gas prices, and declining consumer sentiment—all of which contributed to more deliberate spending behavior. Higher beef costs also weighed on the quarter, with Applebee’s commodity costs up 8.2 percent year-over-year.

> “Guests aren’t walking away from dining out, but they are making intentional choices of when and where they choose to go.” —Dine Brands CEO John Peyton

Dine continues to lean on value-driven offerings to help alleviate some of that pressure, with Applebee’s 2 for $25 platform accounting for 26 percent of sales mix in the quarter, and IHOP’s everyday value menu representing 22 percent.

At Applebee’s, that meant pairing its All You Can Eat offer with more premium promotions, including its Poolio with Don Julio campaign. The beverage-focused activation helped liquor sales rise 10.5 percent during the promotion. Introducing the Loaded Potato Waves became the chain’s strongest appetizer launch since the pandemic, providing another traffic and check-building tool as Applebee’s headed into the second half.

“This is our barbell strategy and our marketing playbook in action,” Peyton said—“an accessible, value-driven, all-you-can-eat campaign anchored in affordability paired with a culturally resonant higher-priced indulgence that drove traffic and generated social buzz among the younger audience.”

The company is also attempting to sharpen the guest experience beyond the menu. Through its “Lookin’ Good” remodel program, Applebee’s completed 66 restaurant renovations year-to-date and expects to finish more than 100 by the end of 2026. Those remodeled locations are generating a mid-single-digit sales lift on average, according to the company, while Applebee’s average Google rating climbed to 4.4 from 4.1 a year ago.

IHOP, meanwhile, outperformed Black Box benchmarks in both sales and traffic for the third consecutive quarter.The chain saw a 1.5 percent same-store sales gain,driven largely by check growth. IHOP took roughly 3.5 percent menu pricing in Q2, while traffic was nearly flat.

At the same time, the breakfast brand saw a 3.5 percent lift in off-premises, delivering its fifth consecutive quarter of positive off-premises comp sales. IHOP’s catering business was also a standout. Comp sales accelerated 22 percent in Q2, up from 16 percent in Q1, reflecting growing demand across occasions beyond the restaurant.

“Guests aren’t walking away from dining out, but they are making intentional choices of when and where they choose to go,” Peyton said.

Dine’s progress on operational improvement was also “tangible,” Peyton said. Table turns at IHOP improved by four minutes compared to the end of last year, a “meaningful throughput gain,” he noted. “And guests are responding. IHOP’s average Google rating rose to 4.0 out of 5 in Q2, up from 3.9 a year ago, while its review base also grew by more than fourfold over the same period, reflecting broader guest engagement and consistent in-restaurant experience.”

“The strategy is working and the operational foundation behind it is stronger than it was a year ago,” he added.

Its menu strategy, too, is balancing everyday affordability with more premium fare. IHOP added a BLT and fries to its $6 value menu, while continuing to push higher-check items like Stuffed ’N Stacked Omelets. The return of Dubai Chocolate Pancakes in the third quarter was already exceeding internal expectations in its first few weeks, Peyton said.

Fuzzy’s Taco Shop also recorded positive comps for the second straight quarter, giving Dine evidence that its value-led strategy and brand-level improvements are gaining traction even as Applebee’s works through a slower start to the year.

The rest of the year will test whether IHOP can sustain its momentum and industry outperformance, and, in the years to come, whether the company’s spending on remodels and dual-brand restaurants can produce meaningful and sustainable growth.

 Oct  2  2026

Glory Days Grill & Sports House has launched GDG Pick’em, a new weekly professional and college football prediction challenge that gives guests a new way to compete with fellow fans, engage with their local Glory Days Grill and earn food and discounts for getting their picks right. The interactive game is part of Glory Days Grill’s ongoing commitment to guest experience and its Victory Club loyalty program, giving members a unique way to engage with the brand throughout the football season. Guests must be Victory Club members to participate and earn rewards through GDG Pick’em.

“Glory Days Grill has always been about bringing people together around great sports and great food, and GDG Pick’em takes that experience a step further for our guests,” said Jen Ulmer, Glory Days Grill’s Chief Marketing Officer. “Whether you’re competing against friends across the booth or climbing your local restaurant’s leaderboard for free food and rewards, it turns passive viewing into an interactive, high-energy experience you can only get at Glory Days.”

Each correct pick earns one point, with participants competing on a leaderboard specific to their Glory Days Grill location. The more correct picks guests make, the higher they climb — and the more they have to play for.

Each week, the top three finishers at participating Glory Days Grill locations can win:

*   **1st Place:** $15 off
*   **2nd Place:** Free 6 Boneless Wings
*   **3rd Place:** Free Cookie Sundae

Guests can make their picks each week and follow their standings throughout the season, turning every weekend of football into another opportunity to compete, earn bragging rights and score something good to eat.

The experience brings together two of the things Glory Days Grill is best known for: sports and food. Unlike a traditional promotion, GDG Pick’em gives guests an ongoing reason to participate, follow the action and check back with their local Glory Days Grill throughout the season. The location-based leaderboards also add a local competitive element, allowing guests to compete directly with other fans in their community.

The program is open throughout the football season, with guests able to participate in both professional and college football picks. In addition to weekly prizes, the program features a season-long competition that gives top performers another opportunity to earn rewards.

Ready to put your picks where your appetite is? Visit GDG Pick’em to create an account, join Victory Club, make your picks and start competing. For complete eligibility requirements, prize details and official rules, visit the GDG Pick’em website.

BJ’s Restaurants CEO Lyle Tick has observed today’s customer dynamic unfolding through a couple of avenues. If you look at the endless string of data reports on the subject, you’d assume, understandably, the diner was under some degree of stress. He views what’s taking shape differently, however: One, is what Tick refers to as “durable and disposable transactions.” The kind of traffic a brand like BJ’s, and other casual-dining chains, competes for falls under this distinction. Or, “the social splurge space.” “Whether it’s the weekly, a couple of times a month, I’m going out with friends. I’m going out with family. It’s an experience-based thing. And I think people protect those things,” Tick said during the Barclays Annual Global Consumer Staples Conference. “Disposable transactions” are occasions more like weekday lunch or grabbing a quick dinner on the way home. Customers, he said, tend to shed such visits in favor of guarding their social trips. “And so, that’s where we compete,” Tick said. “That’s where we do well. And I think that’s potentially a dynamic why we’re doing well.” It’s a present landscape, he continued, favoring some of BJ’s peers (like Chili’s) where a spread of winners and losers has formed among full-service chains; a time where consumers, when they do decide to open their wallets, are prioritizing a great exchange for their dollars. The brands thriving, Tick said, are those investing in their value proposition holistically. “Their product, their service, their atmosphere, and making sure they have a place where their team members and their guests want to be,” he said. “And those folks are winning more. I think, thankfully, over the past couple of years, we’ve made pretty significant progress across those areas.” This larger macro picture might be fueling BJ’s, but it’s merely a piece of much-larger jigsaw for a brand coming off one of its best periods in years. The chain posted same-store sales growth of 6.5 percent in Q2 as traffic leapt 8.3 percent. It marked BJ’s eighth consecutive run of comps and traffic growth and the loftiest comps bump in three years and highest traffic in four. Mother’s and Father’s Day sales spiked north of 8 and 3 percent, respectively, year-over-year, and more than 80 stores broke daily or weekly records. And regarding Tick’s notion of a pressured consumer, BJ’s didn’t feel it—it notched growth through all geographies, dayparts, and channels. Sales increases were evenly distributed across the week as well. Again, he feels guests are simply doing what they have to so they can socialize and indulge. BJ’s is there to fill that need-state when it arises. And in recent quarters, as Tick, who was named CEO last June after serving as president and chief concept officer (he was formerly brand president of Buffalo Wild Wings from 2018 to 2023), kept sharing industry-fronting results with investors, he was often asked to compartmentalize BJ’s success. ![Image 65: BJ's restaurant exterior.](https://www.fsrmagazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/bjsrestaurants-1024x597.jpg) Bj’s has been on a sales and traffic run. In other terms, was there one thing driving the surge? That’s a byproduct of life on Wall Street, where analysts value quarter-to-quarter recaps as much as long strips of growth. Tick said, from his view, it doesn’t quite work that way. BJ’s doesn’t have a “one thing” to explain its upturn. Over the past two years, it’s been a combination of foundation-setting plans alongside marketable wins, starting with operations. Pillar fixes showed in guest and employee metrics, Tick said. BJ’s then followed by unlocking “the power of the Pizookie,” building an everyday value platform, improving product—beginning with pizza—and moving through burgers and its chicken sandwich. Also, “putting a fair bit” of money back into facilities and driving BJ’s remodel program. During this multi-year stretch, the brand added $500,000 on the average-unit volume line, roughly $220,000 of restaurant-level cash flow, and expanded margins 240 basis points. “You get, kind of the ‘we want you to be building a long-term better business and then it’s, but what happened this quarter?’ And I think we try and be really focused on building a better business over time,” Tick said. Todd Wilson, EVP and CFO, added BJ’s trajectory has inspired investors to ask about development. The brand, flat year-over-year at 219 units, is looking to open two stores this year as it focuses on internal unit-level economics. Still, he said, BJ’s is actively seeking new sites, signing leases, and negotiating with landlords. “And so, the proof points are over the last eight quarters of same-store sales growth, traffic growth, dollar and margin expansion that we’re building the pipeline,” he said. “[It] just takes some time when you’re talking 12- to 24-month lead times.” **Trends in the trenches, and traffic-boosting ideas** Tick fielded a question on GLP-1s. His answer wasn’t unlike the opening point around consumer discretion. BJ’s was recently conducting a market test for shareable sides. Which one outperformed the pack? The most decadent, over-the-top feature. “And I remember hearing a Delta chef talk about, he puts healthy things on the Delta menu and everybody gets the steak and the potatoes,” he said. “And so, I think, what people say and what they do can be a little different. I do think our occasion—that social splurge occasion—is a little insulated.” More broadly, Tick believes customers are focused on finding real food, cooked fresh and made well. That’s something BJ’s is hyper-attentive about as it innovates through categories. A lot of BJ’s wide-ranging menu is from-scratch. Going forward, as it evolves sections, it’s asking how to focus on being scratch “where it matters, fresh, real, made-for-you food that makes people feel good about the stuff they’re putting in their body,” Tick said. “I think over time that’s going to continue to be true as long as it’s craveable,” he added. “I haven’t seen anything that has people choosing something healthy that isn’t craveable.” The core of BJ’s business surrounds food, product, and menu. Like he shared, Tick circled pizza, burgers, and chicken sandwiches as areas of need after being elevated to the role. With all the chatter around technology and innovation, what BJ’s serves will always be the conversation that gets Tick the most excited, he said, and a continual journey. “We’re a restaurant company, right?” he said. But as culinary work matures, BJ’s refined a fresh prototype and its brand standards, as well as how the company expresses who it is—all things that will crystalize as BJ’s heads into next year and builds a proof of concept with the store. Changes will manifest in physical buildings and BJ’s total experience, from menus and engineering to plateware and cutlery. ![Image 66:

The Spooky Pizookie is available beginning September 28 and made of a darker-than-night Cookies ’N’ Cream cookie topped with Oreo crumbs and ghoulish Halloween sprinkles. 

](https://www.fsrmagazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/BJ-1024x597.jpg) The Spooky Pizookie. **The road here and what’s ahead** The brand reached this inflection by starting at the center. Tick said BJ’s knows customers who visit thanks to seasonal Pizookie launches show up again. [And like some of the comments made by Chili’s in past months around turning trial via core items into lasting gains](https://www.fsrmagazine.com/feature/how-chilis-plans-to-remain-americas-hottest-restaurant-brand/), Tick wanted to use Pizokies as a way to reintroduce customers to a better restaurant. “And therefore, as we bring new people in, in theory, some of those people are going to have a good time and become customers. So, there’s a flywheel there,” he said. When seasonal Pizookies hit a nerve (the current is a Spooky version with Halloween sprinkles), like they did in Q2 (in that case a Biscoff option), they resonate in particular with young customers, like high school and college kids, Tick said. “Recruiting that next generation into our restaurant,” he said, “I’ll take that every day of the week.” Internally, BJ’s covers a dynamic it calls “Pizookie trial checks.” You’ll see a bunch of appetizers, Pizookies, and some drinks. These aren’t discounted checks necessarily, but from a dollar amount they’re lower than normal orders. Importantly, though, they’re a sign people are discovering BJ’s. The brand has a $13 Pizookie Meal Deal that, likewise, drives acquisition and repeat visits. Tick said, when he unpacks overall performance, sales for BJ’s have been consistent. It’s not evolving toward a “lumpy business” where it’s only growing during discount days or special launches. Wilson added, over the past year or so, mix shows customers gravitating to areas of the menu the company highlighted. Guests are ordering the pizza BJ’s reinvented last fall, burgers upgraded earlier this year, and the chicken sandwiches fine-tuned more recently. It’s pulled some people out of higher-priced items like steaks and Slo Roast. Yet all are benefiting categories from a sales and margin angle. “As you look forward, it gives us confidence that as we reinvent those future sections, we’ll be able to push people back there to items that, one, they certainly enjoy and have higher satisfaction, and two, that have favorable business financials for us,” Wilson said. Pizza represents about 6–7 percent of BJ’s sales mix, but touches 20 percent of checks. Tick said the brand ideated there because, as shown, it’s on a lot of orders. But also, it’s BJ’s founding product and something he didn’t feel it could afford to let guests down on. “I’m a brand guy,” he said. “So, I start from, are we clear in our brand positioning? Are we clear in our consumer” And then, is your foundation strong?” Guest satisfaction in pizza had been eroding. Sales were lagging. BJ’s had to get its day one equity renovated before it could look at burger, handhelds, etc. Between those three categories (burgers, pizza, chicken sandwiches), it’s about 25 percent of sales. # The Flying Biscuit Café Inks Franchise Deal in Katy, Texas

 Aug  24  2026 

 Industry News 

Share:

[Tweet](https://twitter.com/share?url=https://www.fsrmagazine.com/industry-news/the-flying-biscuit-cafe-inks-franchise-deal-in-katy-texas/&text=The%20Flying%20Biscuit%20Caf%C3%A9%20Inks%20Franchise%20Deal%20in%20Katy%2C%20Texas "Share on Twitter")[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.fsrmagazine.com/industry-news/the-flying-biscuit-cafe-inks-franchise-deal-in-katy-texas/&display=popup&ref=plugin&src=share_button "Share on Facebook")[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https://www.fsrmagazine.com/industry-news/the-flying-biscuit-cafe-inks-franchise-deal-in-katy-texas/ "Share on LinkedIn")[Email](mailto:?subject=Your%20friend%20has%20shared%20an%20article%20with%20you.&body=The%20Flying%20Biscuit%20Caf%C3%A9%20Inks%20Franchise%20Deal%20in%20Katy%2C%20Texas%0D%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fwww.fsrmagazine.com%2Findustry-news%2Fthe-flying-biscuit-cafe-inks-franchise-deal-in-katy-texas%2F%0D%0A "Share via Email")

The Flying Biscuit Café has signed a franchise agreement to bring the Atlanta-born all-day breakfast and brunch brand to Katy, Texas, with longtime guests Mario and Ifeoma Harper signing a single-unit franchise agreement to open the brand’s first café in Katy. The agreement adds to Flying Biscuit’s established Houston-area footprint, where the brand already operates five cafés — in Memorial City, East Downtown, Kingwood, Richmond, and Cypress.

A site has not yet been selected. The Harpers are working with the Flying Biscuit development team on real estate in the Katy area, and the location and opening timeline will be announced once a lease is signed.

For the Harpers, the decision started on the guest side of the counter. The couple, who live in the Houston area, have been regulars at the brand’s Memorial City café for years, and looked at several concepts before choosing Flying Biscuit. They pointed to the strength of the corporate support structure and the opportunity in their own backyard as the deciding factors.

Mario Harper is an attorney and entrepreneur with a background in supply chain, small business investment, and real estate. Ifeoma Harper brings 25 years in commercial banking, advising middle-market and corporate clients on capital strategy and growth.

“We chose Flying Biscuit because it’s a truly special breakfast concept — those fluffy biscuits and bold, comforting flavors that people genuinely come back for,” said Mario Harper, Flying Biscuit Café franchisee. “We’re most excited to bring that warm, satisfying experience to Katy and make it a neighborhood favorite — a go-to spot for brunch on the weekend and breakfast the rest of the week.”

Katy is one of the fastest-growing communities in the Houston metro, and the café will fill in the map between Flying Biscuit’s Richmond café to the south and Cypress to the north — the same family traffic and weekend routines that have worked for the brand across the rest of Houston.

Flying Biscuit serves breakfast, brunch, and lunch, with cafés closing in the afternoon. The menu runs to Southern-inspired takes on brunch standards — stuffed French toast, the brand’s famous shrimp and grits, hearty omelets, vegan scrambles, burgers, and wraps — and many locations offer a full bar with brunch-forward cocktails.

# The Flying Biscuit Café Signs Lease for First Location in Abilene, Texas

 Aug  19  2026 

 Industry News 

Share:

[Tweet](https://twitter.com/share?url=https://www.fsrmagazine.com/industry-news/the-flying-biscuit-cafe-signs-lease-for-first-location-in-abilene-texas/&text=The%20Flying%20Biscuit%20Caf%C3%A9%20Signs%20Lease%20for%20First%20Location%20in%20Abilene%2C%20Texas "Share on Twitter")[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.fsrmagazine.com/industry-news/the-flying-biscuit-cafe-signs-lease-for-first-location-in-abilene-texas/&display=popup&ref=plugin&src=share_button "Share on Facebook")[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https://www.fsrmagazine.com/industry-news/the-flying-biscuit-cafe-signs-lease-for-first-location-in-abilene-texas/ "Share on LinkedIn")[Email](mailto:?subject=Your%20friend%20has%20shared%20an%20article%20with%20you.&body=The%20Flying%20Biscuit%20Caf%C3%A9%20Signs%20Lease%20for%20First%20Location%20in%20Abilene%2C%20Texas%0D%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fwww.fsrmagazine.com%2Findustry-news%2Fthe-flying-biscuit-cafe-signs-lease-for-first-location-in-abilene-texas%2F%0D%0A "Share via Email")

The Flying Biscuit Café has signed a lease for its first café in Abilene, Texas, at 2467 N Judge Ely Blvd., bringing the Atlanta-born all-day breakfast and brunch brand to West Texas for the first time. The café will be the brand’s first in Texas outside the greater Houston area.

The café will occupy space at Allen Ridge, an approximately 30,000-square-foot dining, retail and entertainment development at the corner of E Ambler Avenue and N Judge Ely Boulevard, just off Interstate 20 and less than a mile from Abilene Christian University.

The café will be owned and operated by franchise partners Edward Ortiz, Samantha Ortiz and Edgar Ortiz. The Ortizes come to the brand as experienced franchise owners, already operating a couple of other franchise businesses — so they know what it takes to build one from the ground up. Flying Biscuit is the concept they wanted to bring home to Abilene.

“We wanted to bring something new to West Texas, and Abilene is home,” said Edward Ortiz, franchise partner. “What matters most is giving friends and families a place to sit a while. We want everyone who walks in to leave planning the next visit — and we’d like Abilene to claim this one as its brunch spot.”

An opening is targeted for the first quarter of 2027, with the date to be announced as buildout progresses.

Real estate representation for the property was provided by ARL Retail, the developer of Allen Ridge.

The Flying Biscuit Café is actively awarding franchise territories across Texas.

# The Flying Biscuit Café Signs Lease in Magnolia, Texas

 Aug  28  2026 

 Industry News 

Share:

[Tweet](https://twitter.com/share?url=https://www.fsrmagazine.com/industry-news/the-flying-biscuit-cafe-signs-lease-in-magnolia-texas/&text=The%20Flying%20Biscuit%20Caf%C3%A9%20Signs%20Lease%20in%20Magnolia%2C%20Texas "Share on Twitter")[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.fsrmagazine.com/industry-news/the-flying-biscuit-cafe-signs-lease-in-magnolia-texas/&display=popup&ref=plugin&src=share_button "Share on Facebook")[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https://www.fsrmagazine.com/industry-news/the-flying-biscuit-cafe-signs-lease-in-magnolia-texas/ "Share on LinkedIn")[Email](mailto:?subject=Your%20friend%20has%20shared%20an%20article%20with%20you.&body=The%20Flying%20Biscuit%20Caf%C3%A9%20Signs%20Lease%20in%20Magnolia%2C%20Texas%0D%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fwww.fsrmagazine.com%2Findustry-news%2Fthe-flying-biscuit-cafe-signs-lease-in-magnolia-texas%2F%0D%0A "Share via Email")

The Flying Biscuit Café has signed a lease for its first café in Magnolia, Texas, at 5667 FM 1488, Suite D, Magnolia, TX 77354. Franchise partners Mitchell and Heather Wagner will own and operate the restaurant, which is scheduled to open in the fourth quarter of 2026.

The site sits on FM 1488, Magnolia’s main commercial corridor, in Magnolia Village, alongside established local businesses.

The Wagners picked Magnolia before they picked a site. Both grew up in small Texas towns, and the two were married at The Meekermark, a few minutes from the new café. They live in the community they’re about to serve.

“We chose Flying Biscuit because it’s more than a restaurant — it’s a place where community comes together over great food and genuine hospitality. Magnolia already holds a special place in our hearts; we were married at The Meekermark here, and we’ve dreamed of putting down roots in this town ever since. Having both grown up in small towns in Texas, we know firsthand how much a place to gather means to a community, and we can’t wait to give Magnolia a spot where families and friends can create memories of their own,” said Mitchell Wagner, franchise partner, The Flying Biscuit Café of Magnolia.

Wagner is a U.S. Army veteran and a graduate of Texas State University. He spent 27 years leading sales and operations for two of the country’s largest retailers, running businesses with more than $100 million in revenue and teams of 300-plus. Heather Wagner joins him as co-owner. The two first ate at a Flying Biscuit on a trip to Charlotte and have been regulars since.

The Wagners plan to build the café around Magnolia’s families, schools, youth sports teams, churches and community organizations, and — as a veteran himself, Mitchell notes — its first responders, active military and fellow veterans. They also intend to join the Magnolia Chamber of Commerce.

Magnolia is the first of two cafés the Wagners have committed to develop under their agreement with the brand.

David J. Littwitz of Littwitz Investments, Inc. and Britton Lankford of The Woodmont Company brokered the transaction.

Magnolia will be Flying Biscuit’s sixth café in Texas, joining five Greater Houston locations: Cypress, East Downtown Houston, Kingwood, Memorial City and Richmond.

The **[early history of cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_cricket_to_1725 "History of cricket to 1725")** began with a children's game in southeast England, possibly traced to [Flemish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flanders "Flanders") immigrants to that area. The earliest definite reference to [cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket") is dated 17 January 1597 ([Old Style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Style_and_New_Style_dates "Old Style and New Style dates")) in a deposition in a legal case regarding the usage of a parcel of land. Around that time, it evolved into an adults' game, and there are many references to it in the 17th century. The earliest-known "big match" was played in [Sussex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sussex "Sussex") in 1697, when the sport was already acquiring wealthy and influential patrons such as [Charles Lennox, 2nd Duke of Richmond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Lennox,_2nd_Duke_of_Richmond "Charles Lennox, 2nd Duke of Richmond")_(pictured)_. They hired the first professional players, and matches were played for high stakes to satisfy gambling interests. During the first quarter of the 18th century, cricket became the foremost sport in England's southeastern counties. By 1725, it was increasingly widespread and became the country's national summer sport. Meanwhile, overseas trade had taken it to both India and North America. _(**[Full article...](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History\_of\_cricket\_to\_1725 "History of cricket to 1725")**)_

**Join the Commons**  

If you don't have a Wikimedia Commons account yet, [create one](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:CreateAccount "Special:CreateAccount") - takes just a few moments!**Find historical sites**  

Find registered historical sites in the United States via **[our guide](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Commons:Wiki_Loves_Monuments_in_the_United_States/Monuments "Commons:Wiki Loves Monuments in the United States/Monuments")**.**Take photos**  

Take photos to document the site, or search through photos you've previously taken.**Describe them**  

Note the site's name, any historic registries it's on, and date of photo.**Upload to Commons**  

Upload your photos through October under a free license.

**Wiki Loves Monuments** is an international photographic competition that invites the global community to document and preserve historic sites around the world on [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/en:Wikipedia "w:en:Wikipedia") and other Wikimedia projects.

A 'monument' refers to a protected historic site that is recognized by a governmental body or other organization, such as a historical society. In the United States, this primarily consists of places listed on the [National Register of Historic Places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places "en:National Register of Historic Places"), which is the United States federal government's official list of districts, sites, buildings, structures and objects deemed worthy of preservation for their historical significance. We also accept photos of historic sites that are recognized by tribal, state, and local governments, as well as historical societies and related organizations.

This year the United States is participating through the month of October. By sharing your photos under a [free license](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Commons:Licensing "Commons:Licensing") that allows anyone to use them, you help document our history and share it with the rest of the world to enjoy through the internet, and get a shot at winning a prize! We will explain below how to participate, what you can win and what monument sites are eligible.

### Participate

Find a registered historic site and upload a photo you have taken of it to the Wikimedia Commons:

[Find a monument»](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Commons:Wiki_Loves_Monuments_in_the_United_States/Monuments "Commons:Wiki Loves Monuments in the United States/Monuments")

[Create an account»](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:CreateAccount "Special:CreateAccount")

[Upload your photos!»](https://wikilovesmonuments.us/upload)

### U.S. Prizes

1st: $500  
 2nd: $300  
 3rd: $200  
 4th–10th: $50 each  
  
Special Prizes  
 Most sites previously unillustrated: $100  
 Top 2 Native American site photos: $50 each  
 Top 2 UAV (drone) photos: $50 each  
See the Prize Categories section below for full details. Monetary prizes will be provided as a gift card of the winner's choice.

## Why participate?

![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/WLM-icon-edit-neg.svg/120px-WLM-icon-edit-neg.svg.png?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)Help Wikipedia document historically significant buildings and historical sites.

![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/00/WLM-icon-camera-neg.svg/120px-WLM-icon-camera-neg.svg.png?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)A nice challenge to improve your photography skills.

![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e6/WLM-icon-prize-neg.svg/120px-WLM-icon-prize-neg.svg.png?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)Compete for prizes in both the national and international competitions.

## Competition rules

There are a few rules for photos to participate in the United States contest.

*   Photos must be your own work.
*   Photos may have been taken at any time (including prior to this event), but must be uploaded during October 2026 to be included in the contest. The US contest formally begins October 1 in US Eastern time (UTC-4) and ends at the end of October 31 in Hawaii-Aleutian Standard Time (UTC-10).
*   During the upload process, you must release your photo under a free license that allows for re-use of the image ([CC BY-SA license](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/) or similar) - see [Commons:Licensing](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Commons:Licensing "Commons:Licensing") for more information.
*   Photos should be **[uploaded through this link](https://wikilovesmonuments.us/upload)** in order to be properly tagged for the contest. 
    *   Experienced contributors may also bypass the portal and manually tag their images [per this guide](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Commons:Wiki_Loves_Monuments_2026_in_the_United_States/Manual_Tagging "Commons:Wiki Loves Monuments 2026 in the United States/Manual Tagging").

*   The photo must feature a site that is identifiable and registered as a historical or cultural site by some authoritative organization (whether on the federal, tribal, state, or local levels). Examples would be the National Register of Historic Places or your local historical society. When you upload your work, be sure to provide the name of the historical site, any identifiers, and the list it is on.
*   Digital manipulations must not deceive the viewer. Correcting flaws, color adjustments, and other minor edits are acceptable.

Next to that, there are a few practical rules:

*   You should have an activated e-mail address on Wikimedia Commons, so that you can be contacted if you win.
*   If the photo gets deleted for any reason, it is automatically disqualified from the competition.
*   You are responsible for following local laws and regulations. 
    *   Do not trespass onto private property.
    *   Be especially careful and ensure you are following regulations when doing drone photography.
    *   Some locations may require a permit for photography.

At the end of the month, the national jury will evaluate the photographs and select winners. See the Prize Categories and Judging sections below for more details.

### Copyright notes

In the United States, you may freely take photos of buildings, but _not_ copyrighted artworks, sculptures, and signage. See [our page on freedom of panorama](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Commons:Copyright_rules_by_territory/United_States#Freedom_of_panorama "Commons:Copyright rules by territory/United States") for more information. Permanently installed artworks may be photographed if they were **installed before 1926**, or **installed before 1978 without a copyright notice**.

Check out [Cornell's guide](https://copyright.cornell.edu/publicdomain) for more details and an easy-to-read table.

Applicable templates:

*   For public artwork installed **before 1926**, use {{[PD-US](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Template:PD-US "Template:PD-US")}} or {{[PD-US-expired](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Template:PD-US-expired "Template:PD-US-expired")}}.
*   For public artwork installed **between 1926 and 1977** inclusive, use {{[PD-US-no notice](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Template:PD-US-no_notice "Template:PD-US-no notice")}} or {{[PD-US-not renewed](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Template:PD-US-not_renewed "Template:PD-US-not renewed")}}.

## Prize Categories

Each year, we recognize our top-ten photos based on composition, technical quality, originality, and usefulness for Wikipedia:

*   1st: $500
*   2nd: $300
*   3rd: $200
*   4th-10th: $50 each

A participant may only place once in the top ten.

The top-ten photos are also submitted to the international competition.

### Special Categories

This year, we have additional prizes for the following categories:

*   Most sites photographed that were previously unillustrated: $100
*   Top two photos of Native American sites: $50 each 
    *   Eligible submissions include photos of recognized tribal properties, historic sites, cultural landmarks, archaeological sites, and monuments that are connected to Native American heritage.
    *   Please note, some Native American nations may require permits for taking photos.

*   Top two UAV (drone) photos: $50 each 
    *   Please ensure you follow laws and regulations when flying a drone. Photos in which the drone operator was violating regulations or creating a hazardous situation will be disqualified.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Part of a personal name

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/75/FML_Names-3.jpg/330px-FML_Names-3.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:FML_Names-3.jpg)

First/given/forename, middle, and last/family/surname with [Edgar Allan Poe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Allan_Poe "Edgar Allan Poe") as example. This shows a structure typical for Anglophonic cultures (and some others). Other cultures use other structures for full names.

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/ff/Desideria_of_Sweden_%26_Norway_grave_2007.jpg/250px-Desideria_of_Sweden_%26_Norway_grave_2007.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Desideria_of_Sweden_&_Norway_grave_2007.jpg)

The sarcophagus at [Riddarholm Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riddarholm_Church "Riddarholm Church") in Sweden of Queen Desideria, an official name given to [Désirée Clary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D%C3%A9sir%C3%A9e_Clary "Désirée Clary") not at birth but when she became [Crown Princess of Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_princess_of_Sweden "Crown princess of Sweden") in 1810.

A **given name** (also known as a **forename** or **first name**) is the part of a [personal name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_name "Personal name")[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Given_name#cite_note-grigg-1991-1) that identifies a person, possibly with one or more [middle names](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_name "Middle name") as well, and differentiates that person from the other members of a group (typically a [family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family "Family") or [clan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clan "Clan")) who have a common [surname](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surname "Surname"). The term _given name_ refers to a [name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Name "Name") usually bestowed at or close to the time of birth, usually by the parents of the newborn. A _[Christian name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian\_name "Christian name")_ is the first name given at [baptism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptism "Baptism").

In informal situations, given names are often used in a familiar and friendly manner.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Given_name#cite_note-grigg-1991-1) In more formal situations, a person's surname may be used. In Western culture, the [idioms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idiom "Idiom") "[on a first-name basis](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/on%20a%20first-name%20basis#English "wikt:on a first-name basis")" and "being on first-name terms" refer to the familiarity inherent in addressing someone by their given name.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Given_name#cite_note-grigg-1991-1)

By contrast, a surname (also known as a family name, last name, or [_gentile_ name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gentile_name "Gentile name")) is normally inherited and shared with other members of one's immediate family.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Given_name#cite_note-2)[Regnal names](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regnal_name "Regnal name") and [religious or monastic names](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_name "Religious name") are special names bestowed upon someone receiving a crown or entering a religious order; such a person then typically becomes known chiefly by that name.

## Name order

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Given_name&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Name order")]

See also: [Personal name §Name order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_name#Name_order "Personal name")

The order _given name – family name_, commonly known as _Western name order_, is used throughout most [European](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe "Europe") countries and in countries that have cultures predominantly influenced by European culture, such as [North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_America "North America") and [South America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America"); [North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_India "North India"), [East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_India "East India"), [Central](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_India "Central India") and [West India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_India "Western India");

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This is a **list of casual dining restaurant chains** around the world, arranged in alphabetical order. A [casual dining restaurant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casual_dining_restaurant "Casual dining restaurant") is a restaurant that serves moderately priced food in a casual atmosphere. Except for [buffet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffet "Buffet")-style restaurants and, more recently, [fast casual restaurants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_casual_restaurant "Fast casual restaurant"), casual dining restaurants usually provide [table service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Table_service "Table service").

## Casual

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_casual_dining_restaurant_chains&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Casual")]

Casual dining usually have waited tables but may have some variations with counter or self service such as buffet.

**DBA** or **dba** may refer to:

## Academic

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=DBA&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Academic")]

*   [Doctor of Business Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_of_Business_Administration "Doctor of Business Administration"), a research-based doctorate degree

## Science and technology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=DBA&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Science and technology")]

### Biology and medicine

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=DBA&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Biology and medicine")]

*   [Diamond–Blackfan anemia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diamond%E2%80%93Blackfan_anemia "Diamond–Blackfan anemia"), a congenital medical condition
*   Dilute, Brown and non-Agouti, a strain of laboratory mice developed by [C. C. Little](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._C._Little "C. C. Little")

### Computing and telecommunication

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=DBA&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Computing and telecommunication")]

*   [DarkBASIC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DarkBASIC "DarkBASIC") (.dba format), a computer language and associated programming environment designed to simplify the creation of 3D video games
*   [Database administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database_administration "Database administration"), a technical function concerned with the effective use and control of a particular database and of its related applications 
    *   [Database administrator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database_administrator "Database administrator"), a person responsible for the environmental aspects of a database

*   [Dynamic bandwidth allocation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamic_bandwidth_allocation "Dynamic bandwidth allocation"), a telecommunications algorithm

### Other uses in science and technology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=DBA&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Other uses in science and technology")]

*   _[Bolkhovitinov DB-A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolkhovitinov\_DB-A "Bolkhovitinov DB-A")_, a 1930s Soviet heavy bomber
*   [dB(A)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DB(A) "DB(A)") or _dBA_, a sound level unit in which different frequencies are weighted differently to account for the perception of the human ear
*   [Design basis accident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Design_basis_accident "Design basis accident"), scenario in nuclear facilities
*   [Dibenzylideneacetone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dibenzylideneacetone "Dibenzylideneacetone"), an organic compound used as a sunscreen
*   [Double Bass Array](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_Bass_Array "Double Bass Array"), active absorption approach for low frequency sound reproduction
*   [Double bend achromat lattice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_bend_achromat_lattice "Double bend achromat lattice"), a magnetic lattice more commonly known as Chasman–Green lattice

## Other uses

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=DBA&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Other uses")]

*   _[De Bellis Antiquitatis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De\_Bellis\_Antiquitatis "De Bellis Antiquitatis")_, a tabletop wargame
*   [Dalbandin Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalbandin_Airport "Dalbandin Airport") IATA code
*   [Dallas Bar Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Bar_Association "Dallas Bar Association"), a professional organization for lawyers in Dallas, Texas, U.S.
*   [DBA (airline)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DBA_(airline) "DBA (airline)"), a former low-cost German airline
*   [Defense Base Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defense_Base_Act "Defense Base Act"), type of insurance that covers employees at U.S. defense bases overseas
*   _[Doing business as](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doing\_business\_as "Doing business as")_, a legal term related to the name a business uses
*   [The Barge Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Barge_Association "The Barge Association"), formerly "Dutch Barge Association" (DBA): a club for leisure users of European inland waterways
*   _[Daredevil: Born Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daredevil:\_Born\_Again "Daredevil: Born Again")_, a 2025 television series produced by Marvel Studios

# Glory Days Grill Launches Weekly Football Pick’em Challenge

 Oct  2  2026 

 Industry News 

Share:

[Tweet](https://twitter.com/share?url=https://www.fsrmagazine.com/industry-news/glory-days-grill-launches-weekly-football-pickem-challenge/&text=Glory%20Days%20Grill%20Launches%20Weekly%20Football%20Pick%E2%80%99em%20Challenge "Share on Twitter")[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.fsrmagazine.com/industry-news/glory-days-grill-launches-weekly-football-pickem-challenge/&display=popup&ref=plugin&src=share_button "Share on Facebook")[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https://www.fsrmagazine.com/industry-news/glory-days-grill-launches-weekly-football-pickem-challenge/ "Share on LinkedIn")[Email](mailto:?subject=Your%20friend%20has%20shared%20an%20article%20with%20you.&body=Glory%20Days%20Grill%20Launches%20Weekly%20Football%20Pick%E2%80%99em%20Challenge%0D%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fwww.fsrmagazine.com%2Findustry-news%2Fglory-days-grill-launches-weekly-football-pickem-challenge%2F%0D%0A "Share via Email")

Glory Days Grill & Sports House has launched GDG Pick’em, a new weekly professional and college football prediction challenge that gives guests a new way to compete with fellow fans, engage with their local Glory Days Grill and earn food and discounts for getting their picks right. The interactive game is part of Glory Days Grill’s ongoing commitment to guest experience and its Victory Club loyalty program, giving members a unique way to engage with the brand throughout the football season. Guests must be Victory Club members to participate and earn rewards through GDG Pick’em.

“Glory Days Grill has always been about bringing people together around great sports and great food, and GDG Pick’em takes that experience a step further for our guests,” said Jen Ulmer, Glory Days Grill’s Chief Marketing Officer. “Whether you’re competing against friends across the booth or climbing your local restaurant’s leaderboard for free food and rewards, it turns passive viewing into an interactive, high-energy experience you can only get at Glory Days.”

Each correct pick earns one point, with participants competing on a leaderboard specific to their Glory Days Grill location. The more correct picks guests make, the higher they climb — and the more they have to play for.

Each week, the top three finishers at participating Glory Days Grill locations can win:

*   **1st Place:** $15 off
*   **2nd Place:** Free 6 Boneless Wings
*   **3rd Place:** Free Cookie Sundae

Guests can make their picks each week and follow their standings throughout the season, turning every weekend of football into another opportunity to compete, earn bragging rights and score something good to eat.

The experience brings together two of the things Glory Days Grill is best known for: sports and food. Unlike a traditional promotion, GDG Pick’em gives guests an ongoing reason to participate, follow the action and check back with their local Glory Days Grill throughout the season. The location-based leaderboards also add a local competitive element, allowing guests to compete directly with other fans in their community.

The program is open throughout the football season, with guests able to participate in both professional and college football picks. In addition to weekly prizes, the program features a season-long competition that gives top performers another opportunity to earn rewards.

Ready to put your picks where your appetite is? Visit GDG Pick’em to create an account, join Victory Club, make your picks and start competing. For complete eligibility requirements, prize details and official rules, visit the GDG Pick’em website.

# The Flying Biscuit Café Signs Lease in Magnolia, Texas

 Aug  28  2026 

 Industry News 

Share:

[Tweet](https://twitter.com/share?url=https://www.fsrmagazine.com/industry-news/the-flying-biscuit-cafe-signs-lease-in-magnolia-texas/&text=The%20Flying%20Biscuit%20Caf%C3%A9%20Signs%20Lease%20in%20Magnolia%2C%20Texas "Share on Twitter")[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.fsrmagazine.com/industry-news/the-flying-biscuit-cafe-signs-lease-in-magnolia-texas/&display=popup&ref=plugin&src=share_button "Share on Facebook")[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https://www.fsrmagazine.com/industry-news/the-flying-biscuit-cafe-signs-lease-in-magnolia-texas/ "Share on LinkedIn")[Email](mailto:?subject=Your%20friend%20has%20shared%20an%20article%20with%20you.&body=The%20Flying%20Biscuit%20Caf%C3%A9%20Signs%20Lease%20in%20Magnolia%2C%20Texas%0D%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fwww.fsrmagazine.com%2Findustry-news%2Fthe-flying-biscuit-cafe-signs-lease-in-magnolia-texas%2F%0D%0A "Share via Email")

The Flying Biscuit Café has signed a lease for its first café in Magnolia, Texas, at 5667 FM 1488, Suite D, Magnolia, TX 77354. Franchise partners Mitchell and Heather Wagner will own and operate the restaurant, which is scheduled to open in the fourth quarter of 2026.

The site sits on FM 1488, Magnolia’s main commercial corridor, in Magnolia Village, alongside established local businesses.

The Wagners picked Magnolia before they picked a site. Both grew up in small Texas towns, and the two were married at The Meekermark, a few minutes from the new café. They live in the community they’re about to serve.

“We chose Flying Biscuit because it’s more than a restaurant — it’s a place where community comes together over great food and genuine hospitality. Magnolia already holds a special place in our hearts; we were married at The Meekermark here, and we’ve dreamed of putting down roots in this town ever since. Having both grown up in small towns in Texas, we know firsthand how much a place to gather means to a community, and we can’t wait to give Magnolia a spot where families and friends can create memories of their own,” said Mitchell Wagner, franchise partner, The Flying Biscuit Café of Magnolia.

Wagner is a U.S. Army veteran and a graduate of Texas State University. He spent 27 years leading sales and operations for two of the country’s largest retailers, running businesses with more than $100 million in revenue and teams of 300-plus. Heather Wagner joins him as co-owner. The two first ate at a Flying Biscuit on a trip to Charlotte and have been regulars since.

The Wagners plan to build the café around Magnolia’s families, schools, youth sports teams, churches and community organizations, and — as a veteran himself, Mitchell notes — its first responders, active military and fellow veterans. They also intend to join the Magnolia Chamber of Commerce.

Magnolia is the first of two cafés the Wagners have committed to develop under their agreement with the brand.

David J. Littwitz of Littwitz Investments, Inc. and Britton Lankford of The Woodmont Company brokered the transaction.

Magnolia will be Flying Biscuit’s sixth café in Texas, joining five Greater Houston locations: Cypress, East Downtown Houston, Kingwood, Memorial City and Richmond.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This is a **list of casual dining restaurant chains** around the world, arranged in alphabetical order. A [casual dining restaurant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casual_dining_restaurant "Casual dining restaurant") is a restaurant that serves moderately priced food in a casual atmosphere. Except for [buffet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffet "Buffet")-style restaurants and, more recently, [fast casual restaurants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_casual_restaurant "Fast casual restaurant"), casual dining restaurants usually provide [table service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Table_service "Table service").

## Casual

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_casual_dining_restaurant_chains&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Casual")]

Casual dining usually have waited tables but may have some variations with counter or self service such as buffet.

This is a [dynamic list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:WikiProject_Lists#Dynamic_lists "Wikipedia:WikiProject Lists") and may never be able to satisfy particular standards for completeness. BJ’s Restaurants CEO Lyle Tick has observed today’s customer dynamic unfolding through a couple of avenues. If you look at the endless string of data reports on the subject, you’d assume, understandably, the diner was under some degree of stress. He views what’s taking shape differently, however: One, is what Tick refers to as “durable and disposable transactions.” The kind of traffic a brand like BJ’s, and other casual-dining chains, competes for falls under this distinction. Or, “the social splurge space.” “Whether it’s the weekly, a couple of times a month, I’m going out with friends. I’m going out with family. It’s an experience-based thing. And I think people protect those things,” Tick said during the Barclays Annual Global Consumer Staples Conference. “Disposable transactions” are occasions more like weekday lunch or grabbing a quick dinner on the way home. Customers, he said, tend to shed such visits in favor of guarding their social trips. “And so, that’s where we compete,” Tick said. “That’s where we do well. And I think that’s potentially a dynamic why we’re doing well.” It’s a present landscape, he continued, favoring some of BJ’s peers (like Chili’s) where a spread of winners and losers has formed among full-service chains; a time where consumers, when they do decide to open their wallets, are prioritizing a great exchange for their dollars. The brands thriving, Tick said, are those investing in their value proposition holistically. “Their product, their service, their atmosphere, and making sure they have a place where their team members and their guests want to be,” he said. “And those folks are winning more. I think, thankfully, over the past couple of years, we’ve made pretty significant progress across those areas.” This larger macro picture might be fueling BJ’s, but it’s merely a piece of much-larger jigsaw for a brand coming off one of its best periods in years. The chain posted same-store sales growth of 6.5 percent in Q2 as traffic leapt 8.3 percent. It marked BJ’s eighth consecutive run of comps and traffic growth and the loftiest comps bump in three years and highest traffic in four. Mother’s and Father’s Day sales spiked north of 8 and 3 percent, respectively, year-over-year, and more than 80 stores broke daily or weekly records. And regarding Tick’s notion of a pressured consumer, BJ’s didn’t feel it—it notched growth through all geographies, dayparts, and channels. Sales increases were evenly distributed across the week as well. Again, he feels guests are simply doing what they have to so they can socialize and indulge. BJ’s is there to fill that need-state when it arises. And in recent quarters, as Tick, who was named CEO last June after serving as president and chief concept officer (he was formerly brand president of Buffalo Wild Wings from 2018 to 2023), kept sharing industry-fronting results with investors, he was often asked to compartmentalize BJ’s success. ![Image 65: BJ's restaurant exterior.](https://www.fsrmagazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/bjsrestaurants-1024x597.jpg) Bj’s has been on a sales and traffic run. In other terms, was there one thing driving the surge? That’s a byproduct of life on Wall Street, where analysts value quarter-to-quarter recaps as much as long strips of growth. Tick said, from his view, it doesn’t quite work that way. BJ’s doesn’t have a “one thing” to explain its upturn. Over the past two years, it’s been a combination of foundation-setting plans alongside marketable wins, starting with operations. Pillar fixes showed in guest and employee metrics, Tick said. BJ’s then followed by unlocking “the power of the Pizookie,” building an everyday value platform, improving product—beginning with pizza—and moving through burgers and its chicken sandwich. Also, “putting a fair bit” of money back into facilities and driving BJ’s remodel program. During this multi-year stretch, the brand added $500,000 on the average-unit volume line, roughly $220,000 of restaurant-level cash flow, and expanded margins 240 basis points. “You get, kind of the ‘we want you to be building a long-term better business and then it’s, but what happened this quarter?’ And I think we try and be really focused on building a better business over time,” Tick said. Todd Wilson, EVP and CFO, added BJ’s trajectory has inspired investors to ask about development. The brand, flat year-over-year at 219 units, is looking to open two stores this year as it focuses on internal unit-level economics. Still, he said, BJ’s is actively seeking new sites, signing leases, and negotiating with landlords. “And so, the proof points are over the last eight quarters of same-store sales growth, traffic growth, dollar and margin expansion that we’re building the pipeline,” he said. “[It] just takes some time when you’re talking 12- to 24-month lead times.” **Trends in the trenches, and traffic-boosting ideas** Tick fielded a question on GLP-1s. His answer wasn’t unlike the opening point around consumer discretion. BJ’s was recently conducting a market test for shareable sides. Which one outperformed the pack? The most decadent, over-the-top feature. “And I remember hearing a Delta chef talk about, he puts healthy things on the Delta menu and everybody gets the steak and the potatoes,” he said. “And so, I think, what people say and what they do can be a little different. I do think our occasion—that social splurge occasion—is a little insulated.” More broadly, Tick believes customers are focused on finding real food, cooked fresh and made well. That’s something BJ’s is hyper-attentive about as it innovates through categories. A lot of BJ’s wide-ranging menu is from-scratch. Going forward, as it evolves sections, it’s asking how to focus on being scratch “where it matters, fresh, real, made-for-you food that makes people feel good about the stuff they’re putting in their body,” Tick said. “I think over time that’s going to continue to be true as long as it’s craveable,” he added. “I haven’t seen anything that has people choosing something healthy that isn’t craveable.” The core of BJ’s business surrounds food, product, and menu. Like he shared, Tick circled pizza, burgers, and chicken sandwiches as areas of need after being elevated to the role. With all the chatter around technology and innovation, what BJ’s serves will always be the conversation that gets Tick the most excited, he said, and a continual journey. “We’re a restaurant company, right?” he said. But as culinary work matures, BJ’s refined a fresh prototype and its brand standards, as well as how the company expresses who it is—all things that will crystalize as BJ’s heads into next year and builds a proof of concept with the store. Changes will manifest in physical buildings and BJ’s total experience, from menus and engineering to plateware and cutlery. ![Image 66:

The Spooky Pizookie is available beginning September 28 and made of a darker-than-night Cookies ’N’ Cream cookie topped with Oreo crumbs and ghoulish Halloween sprinkles. 

](https://www.fsrmagazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/BJ-1024x597.jpg) The Spooky Pizookie. **The road here and what’s ahead** The brand reached this inflection by starting at the center. Tick said BJ’s knows customers who visit thanks to seasonal Pizookie launches show up again. [And like some of the comments made by Chili’s in past months around turning trial via core items into lasting gains](https://www.fsrmagazine.com/feature/how-chilis-plans-to-remain-americas-hottest-restaurant-brand/), Tick wanted to use Pizokies as a way to reintroduce customers to a better restaurant. “And therefore, as we bring new people in, in theory, some of those people are going to have a good time and become customers. So, there’s a flywheel there,” he said. When seasonal Pizookies hit a nerve (the current is a Spooky version with Halloween sprinkles), like they did in Q2 (in that case a Biscoff option), they resonate in particular with young customers, like high school and college kids, Tick said. “Recruiting that next generation into our restaurant,” he said, “I’ll take that every day of the week.” Internally, BJ’s covers a dynamic it calls “Pizookie trial checks.” You’ll see a bunch of appetizers, Pizookies, and some drinks. These aren’t discounted checks necessarily, but from a dollar amount they’re lower than normal orders. Importantly, though, they’re a sign people are discovering BJ’s. The brand has a $13 Pizookie Meal Deal that, likewise, drives acquisition and repeat visits. Tick said, when he unpacks overall performance, sales for BJ’s have been consistent. It’s not evolving toward a “lumpy business” where it’s only growing during discount days or special launches. Wilson added, over the past year or so, mix shows customers gravitating to areas of the menu the company highlighted. Guests are ordering the pizza BJ’s reinvented last fall, burgers upgraded earlier this year, and the chicken sandwiches fine-tuned more recently. It’s pulled some people out of higher-priced items like steaks and Slo Roast. Yet all are benefiting categories from a sales and margin angle. “As you look forward, it gives us confidence that as we reinvent those future sections, we’ll be able to push people back there to items that, one, they certainly enjoy and have higher satisfaction, and two, that have favorable business financials for us,” Wilson said. Pizza represents about 6–7 percent of BJ’s sales mix, but touches 20 percent of checks. Tick said the brand ideated there because, as shown, it’s on a lot of orders. But also, it’s BJ’s founding product and something he didn’t feel it could afford to let guests down on. “I’m a brand guy,” he said. “So, I start from, are we clear in our brand positioning? Are we clear in our consumer” And then, is your foundation strong?” Guest satisfaction in pizza had been eroding. Sales were lagging. BJ’s had to get its day one equity renovated before it could look at burger, handhelds, etc. Between those three categories (burgers, pizza, chicken sandwiches), it’s about 25 percent of sales. Wilson explained, however, one of BJ’s strengths is its large menu. Meaning, there’s plenty of whitespace to keep making changes. Tick said steaks and Slo Roast is a bucket BJ’s is now spending a lot of time on. Similarly, they’re core to the brand and touch a lot of checks. There’s work taking place with salads, too, and soon, specialty entrees. “Were going to touch every category of the menu over the next 12 to 18 months as we ultimately look to get to a menu that we feel like holistically is a more compelling offering,” he said. Circling back, Tick explained a lot of what’s showing up in performance, on milestones like Mother’s and Father’s Day, and otherwise, is operational rooted. COO Christpher Pinsak, promoted in January (he was EVP and chief restaurant operations officer since September 2024 and SVP of operations from January 2010 to then), has keyed on ensuring stores had clean shoulder periods. So, coming out of dayparts, not creating false waits, and moving people through full hands, in and out of the kitchen; making sure tables were never un-bussed for more than a “couple of minutes,” and, plainly, creating a sense of urgency and hustle inside locations. On top, Tick said, BJ’s talked about how about a third of restaurants touted an activity-based labor model, which is an AI forecasting tool centered on getting the right employees in the right place at the right time. That informed BJ’s it needed more people during peak hours and less in nonpeak to push throughput and optimize volume coming through restaurants. And then, Tick continued, shoring up smaller things, like how employees entered orders and sequencing on the KDS. ![Image 67: BJ's Classic Ribeye.](https://www.fsrmagazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/bjsribeye-1024x597.jpg) BJ’s Classic Ribeye. “There’s a constant feedback loop with our GMs, with our executive kitchen managers as we’re optimizing how things come from the front of house into the back of house and then come back through,” Tick said. “And it’s a continual improvement process. But the thing that’s exciting is, again, you see our heavy hitters being able to churn more traffic and churn more volume. And so, it just gives you a sense of how high is up.” BJ’s is also devising ways to grow its loyalty base. Those customers today bump average frequency from just under two visits a year to closer to four. Tick said there are myriad benefits, naturally, including learning about core users and understanding how to cater to them. It also unravels a clearer picture of who the BJ’s loyalist is and how the company might be able to do lookalike targeting outside of restaurants. BJ’s made a change last year after noticing the sign-up hook—get a free Pizookie immediately—was driving trial but not necessarily second visits. BJ’s tweaked to where users earned the offer on their next trip. That resulted in fewer sign-ups, Tick said, but more people returning “a lot more often.” He noted it’s evened out and BJ’s is growing its active loyalty pool again (a group of people transacting within six to 12 months). That, Tick said, is what BJ’s wants to drill down on. How many users are in the program can often be a vanity metric. BJ’s wasn’t doing the best job asking customers about loyalty, from a server script of view. It waited until the end of meals, which Tick felt was a missed opportunity to make a customer feel recognized and important before they ordered. “When you go and ask about it at the end of the meal, if somebody has already decided, I want my check and I want to go, they’re not at that point going to want to sign up and go through the process and give you their phone number and do all of that,” he said. So, BJ’s flipped the script, so to speak. And it’s sparked a boon of sign-ups. “It’s funny how much just the execution at the restaurant and some of that sequencing can make a big difference,” Tick said. ## Applebee’s Franchise Costs: Estimated Initial Investment (Item 7, 2021 FDD)

*   The following table shows the franchisor’s current estimates of the initial investment likely to be required for the development and opening of Applebee’s newest Restaurant prototype.

*   The low range of the costs in the table typically reflects the franchisor’s estimate of costs for a 169-seat version of the newest prototype.

*   The high range of the costs in the table typically reflects the franchisor’s estimate of costs for a 225-seat version of the newest prototype and also takes into account some add-ons that may increase the investment cost, including enhanced fire alarm systems, pylon signs, and costs relating to expanding the Restaurant to accommodate up to 275 seats.

*   The figures in the table reflect the franchisor’s estimate of your initial investment from the time you sign a Development Agreement through approximately 3 months after you open your first Restaurant.

*   The total estimated initial investment includes pro-rated costs and expenses related to on-line ordering, wi-fi services, digital products service fee, server tablet maintenance fee, gateway processing fee, Waitlist, campaign/menu training, and training for 3 months.

*   The estimates for construction costs are based on the most recent costs or on the expected costs for franchisees’ Restaurants to be opened in 2020.

**1. Initial Organizational and Training Expenses (incorporation, legal and accounting fees, training, site location, and miscellaneous expenses): $75,000 to $120,000**

**2. Purchase of Land: $300,000 to $2,000,000**

*   The cost to purchase land varies because of geographic location. If you do not purchase the land and building for the Restaurant, you will need to lease this property, in which case a security deposit may be required.

*   Typical annual rents, which vary widely depending on factors like size, location, and condition of the leased premises, may range from 4% to over 8% of the Restaurant’s Gross Sales per year.

*   Also, you might incur certain construction or remodeling costs for necessary leasehold improvements.

*   Free-standing Restaurant sizes using the newest prototype range from approximately 4,500 square feet (seating 168) to approximately 5,410 square feet (seating 225), and Restaurants located in strip centers, shopping centers, and malls generally require more square footage to achieve the same seating.

**3. Building Costs (purchase, construction, remodeling, etc.): $556,000 to $2,600,000**

# ‘Situation is unfortunate’: Multiple Applebee’s restaurants suddenly close overnight

Close

Multiple Applebee’s restaurants across the Kansas City metro area suddenly closed this week. (Source: KCTV)

By [Sarah Motter](link_81) and [Jordan Gartner](link_82)

Published: Oct. 31, 2024 at 12:46 AM UTC

Share

[Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google](link_83)

KANSAS CITY, Mo. ([KCTV](link_84)/Gray News) - Multiple Applebee’s restaurant locations across the Kansas City metro area have suddenly closed.

Many [Applebee’s](link_85)employees in Kansas City woke up Wednesday morning to the news of the sudden restaurant closings.

Company officials confirmed the closures and said the locations affected were independently owned.

“Applebee’s restaurants are independently owned and operated by franchisees. The closure of eight restaurants in the Kansas City market looks to be the result of financial circumstances and decisions made by the franchisee,” Applebee’s President Tony Moralejo said. “This situation is unfortunate, and we continue to believe the Kansas City area is a great neighborhood for Applebee’s restaurants.”

Moralejo continued, “Two Applebee’s restaurants continue to serve our guests in the Kansas City area.”

Company officials noted that while they typically do not discuss individual franchisees, this particular entity has had periods when they have not been in good standing with the brand and has proven to not represent the brand well in the Kansas City market.

The two Applebee’s restaurants that remain open in the area are the Blue Springs and Gladstone locations.

# ‘Situation is unfortunate’: Multiple Applebee’s restaurants suddenly close overnight

Close

Multiple Applebee’s restaurants across the Kansas City metro area suddenly closed this week. (Source: KCTV)

By [Sarah Motter](link_81) and [Jordan Gartner](link_82)

Published: Oct. 31, 2024 at 12:46 AM UTC

Share

[Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google](link_83)

KANSAS CITY, Mo. ([KCTV](link_84)/Gray News) - Multiple Applebee’s restaurant locations across the Kansas City metro area have suddenly closed.

Many [Applebee’s](link_85)employees in Kansas City woke up Wednesday morning to the news of the sudden restaurant closings.

Company officials confirmed the closures and said the locations affected were independently owned.

“Applebee’s restaurants are independently owned and operated by franchisees. The closure of eight restaurants in the Kansas City market looks to be the result of financial circumstances and decisions made by the franchisee,” Applebee’s President Tony Moralejo said. “This situation is unfortunate, and we continue to believe the Kansas City area is a great neighborhood for Applebee’s restaurants.”

Moralejo continued, “Two Applebee’s restaurants continue to serve our guests in the Kansas City area.”

Company officials noted that while they typically do not discuss individual franchisees, this particular entity has had periods when they have not been in good standing with the brand and has proven to not represent the brand well in the Kansas City market.

The two Applebee’s restaurants that remain open in the area are the Blue Springs and Gladstone locations.
