# Multiple Applebee’s locations close in the Kansas City metro

Close

Multiple Applebee’s locations across the Kansas City metro closed seemingly overnight as employees woke to find news of the closures in their inboxes.

By [Sarah Motter](link_87)

Published: Oct. 30, 2024 at 6:36 PM UTC

Share

[Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google](link_88)

KANSAS CITY, Mo. (KCTV) - Multiple Applebee’s locations across the Kansas City metro closed seemingly overnight as employees woke to find news of the closures in their inboxes.

As many [Applebee’s](https://www.applebees.com/en/menu?utm_medium=cpc&utm_source=Google&utm_content=cpc&utm_campaign=Menu&&&&&gad_source=1&gclid=Cj0KCQjwsoe5BhDiARIsAOXVoUsSkDQ0EK7dQk9UKhOQk8JIipKst_ukXz8rJrLFEJsVs4nicnKdlMsaAmr1EALw_wcB&gclsrc=aw.ds)employees across the metro awoke on Wednesday morning, Oct. 30, news they may need to find a new job started to fill their inboxes. However, the company said the closures were not sanctioned by the brand.

“Applebee’s restaurants are independently owned and operated by franchisees. The closure of eight restaurants in the Kansas City market look to be the result of financial circumstances and decisions made by the franchisee,” said Applebee’s President Tony Moralejo. “This situation is unfortunate, and we continue to believe the Kansas City area is a great neighborhood for Applebee’s restaurants. We are exploring options about the future of these restaurants. Two Applebee’s restaurants continue to serve our guests in the Kansas City area.”

Company officials noted that while they typically do not discuss individual franchisees, this particular entity has had periods of time when they have not been in good standing with the brand and has proven to not represent the brand well in the Kansas City market.

KCTV5 has called various Applebee’s locations in the metro area and has received responses from employees at the Blue Springs location, 1100 NW Highway 7, and the Gladstone location, 6069 NE Antioch Rd., that both remain open.

# Travel & Places

## Embark on a virtual journey to explore travel destinations, cultural landmarks, and geographical wonders. Whether you're a seasoned traveler or planning your first trip, you'll find invaluable tips and insights to make your journey memorable.

[Air Travel Soar through the complexities of air travel, a subject that covers everything from booking flights and seat selection to navigating airports and in-flight amenities. Gain insights into airline policies, frequent flyer programs, and tips for making your air travel experience as smooth as possible.](https://www.answers.com/air-travel)

[Cruises Set sail into the luxurious world of cruises, a subject that offers a deep dive into this all-inclusive travel experience. Learn about different types of cruises, from river cruises to ocean voyages, as well as the amenities, activities, and destinations that make cruising a unique way to explore the world.](https://www.answers.com/cruises)

[Distances and Travel Times Master the logistics of travel with a subject that focuses on distances and travel times. Learn how to estimate the duration of trips, whether by car, plane, or train, and gain insights into tools and resources that can help you plan your itineraries more effectively.](https://www.answers.com/distances-and-travel-times)

[Luggage Dive into the practical aspects of travel with a subject dedicated to luggage. Explore the types, sizes, and features of travel bags and suitcases, as well as tips for packing efficiently and guidelines for airline baggage policies. Learn how to choose the right luggage for different types of trips and how to handle common luggage issues.](https://www.answers.com/luggage)

[Public Transportation Gain insights into the world of public transportation, a subject that covers the various modes of transit that make travel accessible and efficient. Learn about subways, buses, trams, and ferries, as well as ticketing systems, schedules, and tips for using public transport in different countries.](https://www.answers.com/public-transportation)

[Specialty Travel Venture into the niche world of specialty travel, a subject that focuses on unique and specialized travel experiences. From adventure travel and eco-tourism to culinary journeys and wellness retreats, discover the various ways to tailor your travels to your specific interests and passions.](https://www.answers.com/specialty-travel)

[Tourist Attractions Step into the world of tourist attractions, a subject that highlights the must-see landmarks, museums, and activities that define a destination. Explore the history, significance, and visitor experiences offered by these attractions, and learn how to make the most of your sightseeing adventures.](https://www.answers.com/tourist-attractions)

[Travel Accommodations Navigate the diverse landscape of travel accommodations, a subject that delves into the various lodging options available to travelers. Whether it's luxury hotels, budget hostels, or vacation rentals, learn about the amenities, pricing, and tips for choosing the perfect place to stay during your travels.](https://www.answers.com/travel-accommodations)

[Travel Destinations Immerse yourself in the allure of travel destinations, a subject that explores the beauty, culture, and unique experiences offered by places around the globe. From bustling cities and historic landmarks to natural wonders and off-the-beaten-path locales, discover what makes each destination a place worth visiting.](https://www.answers.com/travel-destinations)

[Travel Information Embark on a journey through the world of travel information, a subject that serves as a comprehensive guide for travelers. From visa requirements and travel advisories to currency exchange and local customs, this subject offers invaluable insights that help you plan and navigate your trips, whether they're for business or leisure.](https://www.answers.com/travel-information)

[Disasters & Emergencies Equip yourself with knowledge about disasters and emergencies, a subject that focuses on the types, responses, and preparedness measures associated with unforeseen crises. [Social Groups & Organizations Navigate the intricate web of social groups and organizations, a subject that examines the various collectives people belong to, whether by choice or circumstance. [Social Issues Delve into the pressing challenges and debates that shape society with a subject focused on social issues. # Social Studies

## Social Studies is the integrated study of multiple fields of social science and the humanities, including history, geography, and political science.

[Gerontology Investigate the multidisciplinary study of aging, focusing on the biological, psychological, and social aspects of growing older, as well as societal attitudes and policies related to aging.](https://www.answers.com/gerontology)

[Educational Theory Delve into the principles and methodologies of education, exploring various teaching philosophies, learning styles, and the impact of technology on modern education.](https://www.answers.com/educational-theory)

[Information Science Explore the organization, retrieval, and dissemination of information, a subject that has become increasingly important in the digital age, covering topics from data management to information technology.](https://www.answers.com/information-science)

[Criminology Examine the study of crime and criminal behavior, focusing on the psychological and social factors that lead to criminal activity, as well as the legal systems in place for crime prevention and rehabilitation.](https://www.answers.com/criminology)

[Archaeology Unearth the secrets of past civilizations through the study of material culture, including artifacts, architecture, and landscapes, to understand their social structures and ways of life.](https://www.answers.com/archaeology)

[Linguistics Investigate the intricacies of human language, exploring its structure, evolution, and social aspects, as well as its role in communication, cognition, and culture.](https://www.answers.com/linguistics)

[Anthropology Investigate human societies and cultures, focusing on social norms, traditions, and development. Anthropology offers a holistic view of human existence.](https://www.answers.com/anthropology)

[Geography Study the physical and human characteristics of Earth's surface, including landscapes, cultures, and environmental issues.](https://www.answers.com/geography)

[Political Science Explore the systems and activities associated with governance, including political theory, international relations, and public policy.](https://www.answers.com/political-science)

[Sociology Examine the structures and dynamics of societies and human behavior. Sociology offers insights into social issues like inequality, race, and gender.](https://www.answers.com/sociology)

[Psychology Investigate the complexities of human behavior, thought processes, and emotions. Psychology applies to various aspects of life, from mental health to organizational behavior.](https://www.answers.com/psychology)

[Religious Studies Explore the beliefs, rituals, and ethical systems associated with various world religions. This subject offers insights into cultural diversity and human spirituality.](https://www.answers.com/religious-studies)

[Philosophy Examine the fundamental nature of reality, existence, and knowledge. Philosophy encourages critical thinking and ethical reasoning.](https://www.answers.com/philosophy)

[Law Understand the legal frameworks that govern society, including criminal law, constitutional law, and international law. This subject is crucial for maintaining social order and justice.](https://www.answers.com/law)

# Can You Own a Chipotle Mexican Grill Franchise?

If you’re considering investing in a fast-casual restaurant, the idea of a Chipotle franchise has probably crossed your mind. With its strong branding, high-quality ingredients, and loyal customer base, Chipotle Mexican Grill is a natural fit for franchise hopefuls. But here’s the twist: you can’t buy a Chipotle franchise.

Chipotle operates under a fully corporate-owned model. That means every location is managed by the company itself, not by independent franchisees. Unlike other fast-casual chains that allow individuals to open and run their locations, Chipotle keeps its entire operation in-house. This approach makes the brand a standout in the fast-casual space, limiting direct ownership opportunities for aspiring franchisees.

In this article, we’ll explore why Chipotle has chosen not to franchise, what that means for investors, and what alternative opportunities exist if you’re interested in owning a similar fast-casual restaurant concept.

## Why Chipotle Doesn’t Franchise (Yet)

[Chipotle has chosen to maintain complete control](https://www.entrepreneur.com/franchises/why-chipotle-wont-franchise/237252) of its restaurants to ensure consistency across every touchpoint, from sourcing to service. The company believes this model protects its brand reputation and allows it to innovate quickly without aligning with hundreds of franchisees.

This decision sets Chipotle apart from many competitors in the fast-casual world, where franchising is the norm. While franchising can accelerate expansion, Chipotle has demonstrated that growing slowly and maintaining operational control can be equally effective. The company’s in-house training and quality control enable it to respond to trends, operational challenges, and customer preferences without unnecessary bureaucracy.

## Alternatives to a Chipotle Franchise

Even if a Chipotle restaurant franchise isn’t an option, there are plenty of alternatives in the fast-casual Mexican grill category. Qdoba, for example, offers franchise opportunities and has a nationwide presence. Other options include Barberitos, Tijuana Flats, and Costa Vida, all of which embrace the franchise model. These brands often feature customizable menus, fresh ingredients, and the efficient service for which Chipotle is also known.

Each of these alternatives comes with its own startup costs, royalty structures, and franchisee support systems. Before diving in, compare what each brand offers regarding marketing assistance, site selection, training, and ongoing operational support. Thorough research into your investment is key to making the right decision.

Additionally, when evaluating these alternatives, it’s essential to assess your financial readiness. The chain has also continued to expand into new markets and boost sales through app orders, delivery, and a streamlined menu.

Chipotle’s emphasis on sustainability and food transparency resonates with modern diners. People trust the brand, and that trust translates into strong unit performance. The company also benefits from a consistent social media presence and a successful loyalty program, which helps maintain customer engagement and drive repeat business.

## Is It Still Worth Investing in the Fast-Casual Restaurant Space?

It can absolutely still be worth investing in the fast-casual restaurant space. It’s continued to perform well, especially since the pandemic. Consumers don’t just want speed and convenience — they also want quality. That balance is precisely what fast-casual concepts deliver to consumers.

Many restaurants in this space rank among[America’s most lucrative franchises](https://www.franchisechatter.com/franchise-chatter-names-americas-most-lucrative-franchises/), demonstrating that the model is successful for both franchisors and franchisees. Another factor to consider is the flexibility these models offer. Many fast-casual franchises adapt quickly to new customer preferences, integrating technology for digital ordering, offering ghost kitchens, or opening nontraditional store formats inside airports or on college campuses. These modern adaptations make the model more resilient in an evolving restaurant landscape.

Look for brands that:

*   Focus on fresh, customizable food;
*   Emphasize efficient operations and minimal waste;
*   Have strong digital tools and customer engagement;
*   Offer transparent costs and support for franchisees.

Using [reliable franchise information resources](https://www.franchisechatter.com/) to compare brands side by side can help you make the right decision for your circumstances. It’s also advisable to review startup costs, royalty fees, marketing support, and the company’s history. If possible, talk to current franchisees and get their honest opinions about their experiences. And most importantly, be realistic about your financial position so you can narrow your options wisely.

Of course, this is also good news for the restaurants specifically serving Mexican food. There are [nearly 50,000 Mexican restaurants](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/market-research-reports/mexican-restaurants-industry/#IndustryStatisticsAndTrends/) across the US, [employing 963,000 staff](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/market-research-reports/mexican-restaurants-industry/#IndustryStatisticsAndTrends/). Around [one in ten restaurants](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2024/01/11/about-1-in-10-restaurants-in-the-us-serve-mexican-food/) in the US now serves Mexican food, and the more restaurants there are, the more people get used to this cuisine.

While a lot of this is driven by the wider population’s adoption of Mexican food, immigration is a factor. Hispanic immigrants provide both demand and supply for Mexican cooking, which dominates the Hispanic restaurant scene. While there are other types of Hispanic restaurants, [none of them makes up more than 1% of the restaurant market](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2024/01/11/about-1-in-10-restaurants-in-the-us-serve-mexican-food/). Mexican food has become the iconic taste of the south.

The development of fusions and variations such as Tex-Mex has further fueled growth. They make it easier for people to try Mexican alongside something else, or to incorporate a Mexican touch into a more familiar meal. Cross-cultural restaurants also add novelty and variety to the dining experience, refreshing people’s interest.

Franchising is common in this sector, with major chains using it to quickly expand and tap into growing demand. Some big-name franchises are based in this sector, offering opportunities for new franchisees.

## The Economics of Mexican Restaurant Franchising

The Mexican restaurant industry had [$96.4 billion in revenues in 2024](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/market-research-reports/mexican-restaurants-industry/#IndustryStatisticsAndTrends/), having [grown by an average of 4.7% per year](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/market-research-reports/mexican-restaurants-industry/#IndustryStatisticsAndTrends/) for the previous five years. That ongoing growth makes it a promising sector for those looking to get into franchising.

The serving style of Mexican restaurants helps. Around [37% of Mexican restaurants are quick service](https://datassential.com/resource/mexican-food-growth-united-states/), the preferred format for franchised restaurants. Serving familiar food quickly and cheaply to people on the go is the foundation for many franchises, with cooking treated less as an art form and more as a standardized process, providing wholesome, familiar food wherever customers go. It’s an approach that’s well-suited to standardization and quick setup, and there’s a reason why so many franchisees end up in the quick service sector. Mexican food adapts well to this high-volume style, which has played a part in its spread.

That said, things are currently more challenging than usual for restaurant franchises. The past few years have seen supply chain disruptions and rises in food prices triggered by a number of factors, including the impacts of the Covid pandemic and climate change. As these costs rise, restaurants have to make tough choices about how much of the cost to pass on to customers, many of whom are struggling financially and might be deterred by price rises. Mexican restaurants tend to [operate at a relatively low price point](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2024/01/11/about-1-in-10-restaurants-in-the-us-serve-mexican-food/), so there’s not a lot of room to soak up the costs.

## Getting Mexican Food Right

A restaurant’s success is very dependent on its location. Quick service restaurants often do well by busy roads or in working districts, where they can sell food to busy people on the move. Foods like tacos that can be easily eaten by hand are particularly good for this.

Other factors also come into play. [The biggest determinant of people’s propensity to dine out is their income level](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/market-research-reports/mexican-restaurants-industry/#IndustryStatisticsAndTrends/), so it’s important when setting up any restaurant to pick a neighborhood with enough wealth to support demand. For Mexican, this might be less about high income customers and more about finding those on a middle income with a bit of cash to spare, who will indulge in taco Tuesday or a Friday night Mexican feast, and who will appreciate an inexpensive dining option.

### 1. Taco Bell

[Taco Bell](https://www.tacobell.com/franchise) is the reigning champion of Mexican fast food in the US and has been growing rapidly in recent years, opening an average of more than 200 new locations each year during the past decade. While most fast-food places have more or less given up on the dollar menu concept, Taco Bell still has a few items that only cost $1, and several more that are priced at $2. The industry is seeing changes, as a [new generation of chefs](https://www.msn.com/en-us/foodanddrink/foodnews/new-generation-of-asian-american-restaurant-owners-using-parents-ingredients-and-their-own-creativity-to-elevate-menus/ar-AA1sn58S) adapts the cuisine passed down to them by their parents, bringing in adaptations based on American dining or fresh ideas from back home, and this adds to the sense that this is the go-to cuisine for those seeking something new.

## Chinese Food

These restaurants present a varied and iconic menu that’s become comfortingly familiar for many Americans, with plenty of choice and options they understand. It’s the most visible face of Asian food.

As a result, the Chinese restaurant industry is big business, worth [$27 billion in 2024](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/market-research-reports/chinese-restaurants-industry/), with an [average growth rate of 4.7% per year since 2018](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/market-research-reports/chinese-restaurants-industry/). Healthy eating seems to be helping Chinese restaurants. They often provide food that’s quick, convenient, and familiar – what consumers look for in quick service restaurants – without the unhealthy image that’s become attached to foods such as burgers. Less salt and fat, as well as more visible vegetables, make this a health-conscious choice.

With powerful and popular flavors such as soy sauce, wasabi, and pickled ginger, Japanese cuisine has become immensely popular in recent decades, spreading alongside Japanese culture and technology. ## Korean Food

Korean restaurants were starting to take off in a big way just before the pandemic, providing a novel alternative to more familiar Asian cuisines. But public health closures and the economic fallout hit them particularly hard. As people cut their spending and reverted to the comfortingly familiar, the number of restaurants [dropped from over 7,500 to 6,700](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1178889/number-of-korean-restaurant-industry-businesses-us/).

A few years later, things are turning around. There was a [10% growth in locations](https://www.circana.com/intelligence/press-releases/2024/south-korean-restaurant-locations-in-the-u-s-grow-10-over-the-past-year-amid-surge-in-demand-for-korean-cuisine/) in the year to September 2024, with larger numbers of both full and quick service restaurants. This is tied into a wider wave of interest in Korean culture, as K-pop and K-dramas take America by storm. Korean sauces, kimchi, and dalgona coffee have all found their fans, while a wider pool of consumers is becoming curious about these novelties.

[36% of Korean restaurants](https://www.circana.com/intelligence/press-releases/2024/south-korean-restaurant-locations-in-the-u-s-grow-10-over-the-past-year-amid-surge-in-demand-for-korean-cuisine/) are concentrated in key markets, leaving many market areas untouched, so there are plenty of territories with no Korean restaurant competition.

## Indian Food

Though Indians make up the second-largest community of Asian Americans, they’ve historically had a relatively small impact on the nation’s cuisine. Indian immigrants are proportionally more likely to be highly skilled professionals taking on specialist jobs, so they haven’t taken up less prestigious jobs such as cooking.

But the rising income and influence of Indian Americans has got this cuisine moving. There are now over [4,100 Indian restaurants in the US](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/market-research-reports/indian-restaurants-industry/), ranging from fast casual to fine dining. Indian restaurants were worth $4.9 billion in 2024, after growing by an [average of 2.1% per year](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/market-research-reports/indian-restaurants-industry/) for the previous five years.

Though Indian food is sometimes served to take out, [three-quarters of sales](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/market-research-reports/indian-restaurants-industry/) are for consumption on the premises. As with Chinese food, many people come to enjoy the dining experience.

[Indo-Chinese cuisine](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-67411824), a fusion that’s popular in India, is also on the rise, providing an extra novelty for those wanting something new. And as the waves of different styles spreading through the Asian restaurant market show, Americans remain ready to keep trying new things.

## The Top Asian Restaurant Franchises of 2026

### 1. Panda Express

[Panda Express](https://www.pandaexpress.com/licensing-opportunities) is a chain of American Chinese restaurants, but the standalone restaurants are company-owned and not franchised. The company does license its brand to non-traditional venues such as airports, universities, military bases, hospitals, casinos, amusement parks, and stadiums. The menu of China-inspired fare is extensive but varies by location.

Founded by Andrew and Peggy Cherng in Glendale, California, in 1983, the company website claims there are more than 2,600 locations (it opened its 2,000th store in 2020), most of which are in the US but also in a variety of other countries (Canada, South Korea, Mexico, United Arab Emirates, Japan, El Salvador, Aruba, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Guatemala, and the Philippines).

### 2. L&L Hawaiian Barbecue

[L&L Hawaiian Barbecue](https://www.hawaiianbarbecue.com/franchise/) offers a mash-up menu of influences, including Chinese, Japanese, Filipino, American, and Korean dishes served in the form of the traditional Hawaiian barbecue plate lunch with two scoops of rice, a creamy macaroni salad, and a hot entrée. There’s even Spam on the menu with Spam Musubi – a slice of grilled spam on rice wrapped in dry seaweed – and Spam Saimin (a noodle soup with Spam and fresh green onions).

Founded by Johnson Kam and Eddie Flores Jr. in Honolulu, Hawaii, in 1976 and franchising since 1991, the number of locations currently stands at 231 (up from the previously reported total of 227), of which seven are company-owned and two are located outside the US.

### 3. Teriyaki Madness

[Teriyaki Madness](https://franchise.teriyakimadness.com/) is a fast-casual Asian concept featuring a menu of nine signature bowls (various chicken, beef, and tofu combinations), four appetizers, five side dishes, and seven different house-made sauces. The company has also been testing a mobile food truck concept that may become a franchisee option.

Founded in 2003 and franchising since 2005, the number of locations has risen rapidly in recent years from 15 in 2014 to the current total of 202 (up from the previously reported total of 187), of which one is company-owned and one is located outside the US.

### 4. WaBa Grill

[WaBa Grill](https://wabagrillfranchising.com/) is a chain of rice-bowl restaurants with a relatively simple menu that includes sweet and spicy chicken bowls and plates, in-house marinated rib-eye steak bowls and plates, Waba (chicken and steak) bowls and plates, plant-based steak bowls and plates, wild-caught salmon bowls and plates, shrimp bowls and plates, and tofu bowls and plates. By [Sarah Motter](https://www.wsmv.com/authors/sarah.motter/) and [Andrew McMunn](https://www.wsmv.com/authors/andrew-mcmunn/)

Published: Jan. 12, 2026 at 1:26 AM UTC

Share

[Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=https://www.wsmv.com)

KANSAS CITY, Mo. ([KCTV](https://www.kctv5.com/2026/01/10/kansas-city-restaurant-issues-warning-after-customer-threatened-kill-staff-including-teen/ "https://www.kctv5.com/2026/01/10/kansas-city-restaurant-issues-warning-after-customer-threatened-kill-staff-including-teen/")/Gray News) – A restaurant in Missouri is warning against violence after they said a customer threatened to kill its staff, including a teenager, over a refund.

[Paul’s Drive In](https://www.paulsdriveinkc.com/) posted on social media that the incident happened on Wednesday night, Jan. 7, at its Blue Ridge Blvd. location.

The restaurant’s management said the customer asked for a refund and became verbally aggressive. The situation then escalated to explicit death threats against multiple workers.

“Last night, our team experienced a situation that crossed a line no service worker should ever have to face,” the restaurant said in the post.

The restaurant said the refund was already being processed when the threats started. It said staff are trained to prioritize safety above all else.

“We want to be very clear: this is not about a refund or a disagreement over food. Those situations happen in the service industry, and we work hard to resolve them calmly and fairly every day,” Co-owner Amanda Fulbright said. “What crossed the line, and what makes this incident especially concerning, were threats of violence that escalated to death threats directed at our employees.”

The restaurant owners said the individual was removed from the property after the transaction was completed.

The restaurant said its security cameras recorded the entire encounter. However, it will not be released as Fulbright said the goal is not to shame the individual, but to protect staff members.

“Let us be absolutely clear: Threatening violence over a food order is not acceptable. Ever,” management said. “It is not ‘passion.’ It is not ‘frustration.’ It is assault under Missouri law.”

Management said the customer has been permanently banned from Paul’s Drive In.

“We go out of our way to take care of our customers, but we will not tolerate threats, intimidation or abuse of our staff, especially our minors,” the post said.

The restaurant said violence against service workers is rising and “it has to stop.”

“Zero tolerance means zero tolerance. Our staff - especially minors - deserve to feel safe at work,” the owners said. “Threats of violence will result in immediate removal, a permanent ban, and law enforcement involvement. If you can’t treat people with respect, Paul’s is not the place for you.”

Fulbright said law enforcement was contacted, and her team continues to work through the appropriate legal channels.

In the coming days, she noted that new in-store signage will be posted to clearly outline the restaurant’s commitment to the respectful treatment of both customers and employees.

According to Fulbright, the signage will also emphasize an important component: “We are proud to employ and protect young workers.”

Fulbright also said the restaurant has been overwhelmed by the support from community members and fellow service industry workers.

“Our hope in speaking out is not to sensationalize what happened, but to help de-normalize abusive behavior toward service workers and to make it clear that kindness and basic decency are the standard—at Paul’s and everywhere," Fulbright said.

# Autism advocacy org calls for federal civil rights investigation into Tennessee Wendy’s manager allegedly tying up staffer

##### The 19-year-old manager was charged last week with simple assault and false imprisonment in connection with the August 30 incident.

By [Chasity Maynard](https://www.wsmv.com/authors/chasity-maynard/)

Published: Sep. 23, 2026 at 7:49 PM UTC

Share

[Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=https://www.wsmv.com)

**What This Story Is About**

*   A nonprofit advocacy group is now calling for a federal civil rights investigation into an incident where a Wendy’s manager allegedly tied up a neurodivergent employee.

**Why It Matters**

*   Americans for Autism Advocacy (AFAA) said their request involved “severe allegations of unlawful discrimination and mistreatment of a neurodivergent employee.” 

**What Happens Next**

*   They have asked the U.S. Department of Justice Civil Rights Division to investigate Wendy’s “concerning potential violations of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 and related federal civil rights statutes.”

**For Context**

*   The 19-year-old manager allegedly told police that she tied up the employee as part of a TikTok trend. 

**Catch Up**

*   [**19-year-old Wendy’s manager who allegedly tied neurodivergent employee to grill arrested on multiple charges**](https://www.wsmv.com/2026/09/18/19-year-old-wendys-manager-who-allegedly-tied-neurodivergent-employee-grill-arrested-multiple-charges/ "https://www.wsmv.com/2026/09/18/19-year-old-wendys-manager-who-allegedly-tied-neurodivergent-employee-grill-arrested-multiple-charges/")
*   [**VIDEO: Neurodivergent worker at Murfreesboro Wendy’s tied to kitchen equipment by manager; family pushing for reopened investigation**](https://www.wsmv.com/2026/09/10/murfreesboro-wendys-neurodivergent-worker-tied-kitchen-equipment-family-pushing-reopened-investigation/ "https://www.wsmv.com/2026/09/10/murfreesboro-wendys-neurodivergent-worker-tied-kitchen-equipment-family-pushing-reopened-investigation/")

MURFREESBORO, Tenn. (WSMV) - A nonprofit advocacy group is now calling for a federal civil rights investigation into an incident where a Wendy’s manager allegedly tied up a neurodivergent employee.

The 19-year-old manager, [Michiko Burton, was charged last week](https://www.wsmv.com/2026/09/18/19-year-old-wendys-manager-who-allegedly-tied-neurodivergent-employee-grill-arrested-multiple-charges/ "https://www.wsmv.com/2026/09/18/19-year-old-wendys-manager-who-allegedly-tied-neurodivergent-employee-grill-arrested-multiple-charges/") with simple assault and false imprisonment in connection with the August 30 incident at the Wendy’s on South Church Street in Murfreesboro.

She reportedly told police she tied her neurodivergent employee to a grill with garbage bags as part of a TikTok trend.

But [Americans for Autism Advocacy](https://www.autismadvocatesus.com/national-autism-advocate-calls-on-aag-dhillon-to-investigate-metro-nashville-wendys-franchisee-following-incident-involving-neurodivergent-worker-bound-to-kitchen-equipment/ "https://www.autismadvocatesus.com/national-autism-advocate-calls-on-aag-dhillon-to-investigate-metro-nashville-wendys-franchisee-following-incident-involving-neurodivergent-worker-bound-to-kitchen-equipment/") is asking the U.S. Department of Justice Civil Rights Division to investigate the incident “concerning potential violations of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 and related federal civil rights statutes.”

> “Every neurodivergent individual who is employed deserves to be treated with dignity and respect by their colleagues. The recent incident at a Wendy’s in Murfreesboro, Tennessee, was both alarming and disgraceful. Restraining a neurodivergent team member’s legs to a kitchen grill, as Ms. Burton did, violates basic standards of human decency. While the Wendy’s franchisee took appropriate action by promptly firing Ms. Burton, a thorough civil rights inquiry remains essential to deter future occurrences. We urge Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon of the Civil Rights Division at the U.S. Department of Justice to launch a full investigation. A federal civil rights probe must serve as a clear warning to prevent employers from permitting such misconduct in any workplace.”
> 
> Americans for Autism Advocacy

[![Image 1](https://cloudfront-us-east-1.images.arcpublishing.com/gray/WCZWEBRKNJC6BHZCWR4ZBCEHIA.png)](https://www.wsmv.com/page/our-apps/)

In a Wednesday letter to the DOJ, the organization’s President and Board Chairman Kyle Maichle asks the federal government to investigate Wendy’s of Bowling Green, Inc. and its parent company, Wendy’s International.

The letter [cites WSMV4’s investigation into the incident](https://www.wsmv.com/2026/09/10/murfreesboro-wendys-neurodivergent-worker-tied-kitchen-equipment-family-pushing-reopened-investigation/ "https://www.wsmv.com/2026/09/10/murfreesboro-wendys-neurodivergent-worker-tied-kitchen-equipment-family-pushing-reopened-investigation/"), including footage obtained by WSMV4 showing the employee tied to the grill. That investigation drew national attention, spurring reports from national publications and [amassing nearly 700,000 views](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rST2gWc-Yqc "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rST2gWc-Yqc") on YouTube.

![Image 2: Video: Murfreesboro Wendy’s worker tied to kitchen equipment — family pushing for reopened...](https://gray-wsmv-prod.gtv-cdn.com/resizer/v2/KIPDMCW36FC4RDZ6JBHUH7WSYI.jpg?auth=5528fe8e268b6978a348ecb320c5af587afc685a1425f0005252c56e02b2cff9&width=980&height=551&smart=true)

Video: Murfreesboro Wendy’s worker tied to kitchen equipment — family pushing for reopened investigation(WSMV)

The AFAA also asked for federal investigators to work with local law enforcement to determine if Burton’s actions should be considered hate crimes.

The group asks all agencies to conduct their investigation in close collaboration with the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission “to raise further awareness of the rights of neurodivergent individuals in the workplace.”

WSMV4 has reached out to Wendy’s for comment.

[![Image 2: Subway Sandwich Photo by Fred @ SG](https://www.franchisechatter.com/wp-content/uploads/2011/07/2756788092_c30caef62b_z.jpg)](https://www.franchisechatter.com/wp-content/uploads/2011/07/2756788092_c30caef62b_z.jpg)

**This annual list of the top sandwich franchises was revised for 2026.**

With their variety, popularity, and convenience, sandwiches make a great basis for a franchise. Right now, the future of this market depends upon the struggles around one dominant brand.

## The State of the Sandwich Industry

Every day, [47% of American adults](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK589471/) eat some sort of sandwich. While [58% of these come from stores](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK589471/), either as ingredients or as completed sandwiches, that still leaves a lot of business for restaurants.

While many fast-food chains do their best business at night, sandwich businesses are more likely to be focused on the lunch rush, providing hardworking Americans with a quick meal to get them through the working day.

Sandwich and sub restaurants are currently worth [$45.2 billion](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/market-research-reports/sandwich-sub-restaurants-industry/) in the US, following average annual growth of 1.8% over the past five years. While growth isn’t expected to stay this high, the industry is still forecast to reach around [$48.5 billion within five years](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/market-research-reports/sandwich-sub-restaurants-industry/). Despite inflation and financial uncertainty, sales have remained strong overall.

Several [sandwich chains have faced closures](https://www.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/dining/2024/09/16/capriottis-sandwich-shop-permanently-closes-jacksonville-restaurant/75239317007/) over the past few years. The pandemic had a mixed impact, thanks to these restaurants’ ability to provide food to go, but its fallout has piled on the pressure. Rising costs for labor and ingredients alongside reduced consumer confidence mean that businesses need to watch their margins.

Nowhere is this more starkly visible than at the best-known sandwich brand, Subway.

## Subway Avoids Going Under

Subway isn’t just the biggest sandwich chain in America, it’s [the biggest quick service restaurant (QSR) chain](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/market-research-reports/sandwich-sub-restaurants-industry/#IndustryOverview/), with [nearly five thousand more outlets](https://www.statista.com/statistics/242883/quick-service-restaurant-chains-by-number-of-restaurants/) than its nearest rival. It dominates the sandwich landscape, with more than [four times as many shops as its next competitor](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/market-research-reports/sandwich-sub-restaurants-industry/#IndustryOverview/). However, it’s not the biggest seller in QSR, where [McDonalds is $20 billion ahead](https://www.statista.com/statistics/242883/quick-service-restaurant-chains-by-number-of-restaurants/) of the pack.

Subway faced difficulties in the early 2020s, [shrinking by 10% over three years](https://www.entrepreneur.com/franchises/roark-capitals-96-billion-subway-acquisition-goes-through/473711). While it stayed the biggest business in sandwiches, prospects for new franchisees didn’t look so good. Investment was sought to right the struggling ship, and private equity firm Roark Capital emerged as a buyer.

[Roark finalized its acquisition of Subway in May 2024](https://www.entrepreneur.com/franchises/roark-capitals-96-billion-subway-acquisition-goes-through/473711). While the equity firm claimed that it didn’t want to change Subway, it’s impossible that this sort of investor would leave the company untouched. The purchase [set billions in debt against the brand’s assets and future earnings](https://www.entrepreneur.com/franchises/this-finance-method-is-key-in-the-95-billion-subway-deal/471506). Commentators have been talking for several years about the damage that these sorts of buyouts can do to a company, as private equity takes strong steps to earn its money back fast.

The nature of the Subway deal means that Roark is likely to keep pushing for expansion, whether or not that’s good for existing franchisees. It will also push franchisees to live up to the detail of contracts, leaving less space to adjust to circumstances. Development deals may be more strictly enforced and costly remodels accelerated as the brand grabs for attention.

Subway has been trying to get quick wins with a [series of marketing innovations](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/subway-launches-footlong-sandwich-deal-153725487.html) such as new sauces. But the most attention-grabbing move was a limited duration deal [offering any footlong sandwich for $6.99](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/subway-launches-footlong-sandwich-deal-153725487.html). These look like signs of success for some, and the company has [returned to Entrepreneur’s Franchise 500](https://www.entrepreneur.com/franchises/directory/subway/282839) at number 199 after several years off the list.

## Uncertainties Ahead

At the same time, there are signs that Roark is applying pressure on Subway franchisees, with [an urgent franchisee meeting in August 2024](https://www.entrepreneur.com/business-news/subway-holds-franchisee-conference-as-sales-plummet/478533) to discuss declining sales. At the same time, tensions rose around the $6.99 footlong deal, with [franchisees pushing back](https://www.entrepreneur.com/business-news/subway-holds-franchisee-conference-as-sales-plummet/478533) because of what it would cost them. This was [followed by further rebellions](https://nypost.com/2024/08/30/business/subway-soda-war-forces-owners-to-choose-pepsi-over-coke-or-risk-losing-franchises/) over the installation of meat slicers and a soft drinks deal that franchisees were ordered to sign without knowing financial details. Relations between franchisor and franchisees are deteriorating.

##### **[📈Dreaming of Multi‑Unit Success? Lock In Prime Territories Before They're Gone.](https://www.franchiseba.com/franchise-opportunities/?utm_source=27A6960)**

[Colin](https://www.franchisechatter.com/2025/10/24/firehouse-subs-franchisee-qa-with-colin-means-clearwater-fl/) started as a team member at 21 and now owns 6 locations in Tampa Bay. [Lisa](https://www.franchisechatter.com/2026/04/24/qa-with-lisa-campbell-sola-salons-franchisee/) came from marketing and built 21 in San Diego. The most successful multi-unit owners move early and secure markets with room to grow. Use our [free tool](https://www.franchiseba.com/franchise-opportunities/?utm_source=27A6960) to search multiple ZIP codes and find franchises where you can still stack locations, before someone else does.  
  

If this sounds familiar, that might be because the sandwich industry was home to one of the most dramatic failures in franchising. Quiznos became the second most popular sandwich chain in America in the early 2000s. But poor treatment of franchisees led to a series of court cases while sales fell and the company collapsed into bankruptcy. Twenty years on from its peak, there are [fewer than 150 Quiznos restaurants](https://wkdq.com/how-many-quiznos-subs-are-still-open-in-indiana/) where once there were thousands.

However hard Roark squeezes, it’s unlikely to ruin Subway as badly as Quiznos ruined itself. But the tensions with franchisees point to a similar pattern, and the leveraged buyout means the pressure is unlikely to let up. There may be plenty of opportunities to set up Subway franchises in the next few years, but potential franchisees should be wary of what that experience will be like.

## Standing Out with Sandwiches

That leaves two paths for entrepreneurs interested in sandwich franchising. Either you can sign up with Subway and take a rough ride in hopes that Roark revives a popular brand, or you can pick another chain in hopes of expanding into spaces where Subway fails. Either way, the tricks for standing out are similar.

Novelty can help in attracting customers, as seen in Subway’s [foot-long holiday cookie for Christmas 2024](https://www.inspiremore.com/subway-is-debuting-a-foot-long-chocolate-christmas-treat-this-holiday-season/), as well as its sauces. Each sandwich brand has its own signature specials, so look for what makes it stand out.

Like many businesses, sandwich shops [perform best in cities](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/market-research-reports/sandwich-sub-restaurants-industry/), with their large consumer base. Working areas can be particularly valuable, due to the lunch trade.

[Pricing is important to competition](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/market-research-reports/sandwich-sub-restaurants-industry/). While high-income customers will pay extra for a good sandwich, cheaper options draw in the mass of sandwich eaters. Food aggregators like DoorDash mean that price competition is more visible and more cutthroat than ever, as it’s easy for consumers to compare prices and switch outlets.

As aggregator sales make up [more than a third of sales for sandwich shops](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/market-research-reports/sandwich-sub-restaurants-industry/#IndustryOverview/), these platforms have to be factored into marketing plans. Their review can benefit stores selling cheaply to large numbers of customers, and this may nudge the industry further that way. Find out from any franchise you’re considering how they work with these companies and how they make the most of them.

Subway isn’t the only player in the sandwich market, but its disproportionate size warps the market. What happens there over the next few years will define the shape of the sandwich industry.

## The Top Sandwich Franchises of 2026

### 1. Subway

[Subway](https://www.subwayfranchise.com/) is the undisputed king of sandwich chains in terms of the number of locations, even though the number of domestic locations has been falling in recent years. Unlike many of the largest restaurant franchises, Subway has never gone public and remains a privately-held company. Subway serves up freshly made-to-order sandwiches, wraps, salads, and bowls to millions of guests every day in more than 100 countries around the world. An ever-changing lineup of menu items, promotions, deals, and well-known athletes from various sports in their ads keep Subway at the top of this list.

Founded by Fred DeLuca and Dr. Peter Buick in Bridgeport, Connecticut, in 1965 and franchising since 1974, the number of locations reached a high of 44,830 in 2016 but has since declined to 35,622 (down from the previously reported total of 36,455), of which none are company-owned and 16,120 are located outside the US.

### 2. Arby’s

[Arby’s](https://arbysfranchising.com/) may be a distant second to Subway on this list, but it’s been growing steadily, if slowly, in recent years. The chain is also holding its ground in refusing to offer any kind of plant-based meat substitute. In fact, its nearly decade-old “We have the meats” slogan represents a doubling-down on the chain’s commitment to real meat on its menu. Arby’s is a legacy brand with real staying power. Franchisees can find a store format to fit almost any location, whether traditional restaurants (freestanding, end-cap, or in-line options) or non-traditional (airports, stadiums, colleges and universities, and more).

Founded in 1964 and franchising since 1965, the number of locations was in decline from 2010-2016 but has since been on the rise and currently stands at a total of 3,570 (down from the previously reported total of 3,613), of which 1,063 are company-owned and 234 are located outside the US.

### 3. Jersey Mike’s Subs

[Jersey Mike’s Subs](https://www.jerseymikes.com/franchise) offers more than two dozen hot and cold sub sandwiches served up on bread (white or whole wheat) baked fresh daily in each store. Any sub on the menu can be ordered Mike’s Way with onions, lettuce, tomatoes, spices (salt and oregano), and the Juice (a mixture of red wine vinegar and olive oil). All the subs on the menu can also be ordered as a salad sub bowl or as a wrap (flour tortilla). Jersey Mike’s commitment to fundraising for both local and national non-profit organizations is truly commendable.

Founded as a single restaurant in Pleasant Point, New Jersey, in 1956 and franchising since 1987, the number of locations has rocketed up over the past 10 years from 710 in 2013 to the current total of 3,13

# 19-year-old Wendy’s manager who allegedly tied neurodivergent employee to grill arrested on multiple charges

##### Michiko Burton allegedly told workers she needed the employee to “stay put” so she could do other work in the back of the restaurant.

By [Jeremy Finley](https://www.wsmv.com/authors/Jeremy-Finley/)

Published: Sep. 18, 2026 at 4:09 PM UTC|Updated: Sep. 18, 2026 at 11:44 PM UTC

Share

[Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=https://www.wsmv.com)

#### **What This Story Is About**

*   A former Wendy’s manager in Murfreesboro, Tennessee, was arrested and charged with simple assault and false imprisonment after allegedly tying a neurodivergent employee to kitchen equipment last month. 

#### **Why It Matters**

*   The case involves an allegation of a vulnerable employee being restrained at work, which was referred to Adult Protective Services and investigated by the Special Victims Unit before resulting in criminal charges.

#### **What Happens Next**

*   Burton was booked into the Rutherford County Adult Detention Center on a $2,000 bond. She is scheduled to appear in General Sessions Court on Oct. 22.

#### **For Context**

*   The arrest follows earlier reporting in which a co-worker recorded video of the employee tied to kitchen equipment with trash bags and the employee’s family pushed for police to reopen an investigation.

MURFREESBORO, TN (WSMV) - Murfreesboro Police Department Criminal Investigations Division detectives arrested a former Wendy’s restaurant manager who admitted to tying a neurodivergent employee to a grill last month.

Detectives served a warrant Thursday, Sept. 19, charging Michiko Burton, 19, with simple assault and false imprisonment, a misdemeanor assault charge.

## Investigation details

A WSMV4 Investigation [first revealed how the neurodivergent employee, who we are not naming, was tied with garbage bags to a grill](https://www.wsmv.com/2026/09/10/murfreesboro-wendys-neurodivergent-worker-tied-kitchen-equipment-family-pushing-reopened-investigation/ "https://www.wsmv.com/2026/09/10/murfreesboro-wendys-neurodivergent-worker-tied-kitchen-equipment-family-pushing-reopened-investigation/"). A worker who documented it on video told us that Burton said she didn’t have time to babysit the employee before tying him.

According to police, on Sept. 6, Murfreesboro police officers spoke with Burton, who said the incident was part of a TikTok trend. Burton admitted she tied a worker, who is neurodivergent, to a workstation at the Wendy’s located on South Church Street (Highway 231 South/Shelbyville Highway) on Aug. 30.

The incident was referred to Adult Protective Services and investigated by detectives with the Special Victims Unit. The investigation led to warrants being obtained for Burton’s arrest.

“This has been an awful traumatic event,” said Isaac Kimes, attorney for the family of the neurodivergent employee. “The young man in the video seen now by millions is not doing well.”

Burton was booked into the Rutherford County Adult Detention Center on a $2,000 bond. A court date is set for Oct. 22 in General Sessions Court.

“The family thinks, and I think anyone would think, that it’s absolutely inappropriate, unsafe, and dehumanizing to tie an employee to a grill. Dave Thomas wouldn’t approve of changing an employee to a grill,” Kimes said.

Kimes said the family is currently considering whether or not to take legal action.

## Prior reporting

The employee’s family had asked Murfreesboro police to reopen an investigation after the video showed the worker tied to kitchen equipment. Nicholus Murphy, a co-worker, recorded the video.

“I actually felt sad for him,” Murphy said. “I actually wanted to cry.”

Murphy said Burton told workers she needed the employee to “stay put” so she could do other work in the back of the restaurant.

Burton told police the incident was a TikTok trend and intended as a joke, according to the report. Murphy and the employee’s family disputed that explanation.

“If there was a TikTok trend, then where’s the TikTok?” Murphy said.

After our story aired, Murfreesboro police interviewed the employee, who told officers he was not upset and was not injured. No charges were filed at that time.

[![Image 1: WSMV](https://gray-wsmv-prod.gtv-cdn.com/resizer/v2/WCZWEBRKNJC6BHZCWR4ZBCEHIA.png?auth=23fedf07a4751bca7e96ba6ecffb6c3945d3c72d0d7829ec2518d69abed10b75&width=980&height=245&smart=true)](https://www.wsmv.com/page/our-apps/)

The family of the neurodivergent employee then asked Murfreesboro police to [reopen their investigation.](https://www.wsmv.com/2026/09/12/murfreesboro-police-reopen-investigation-into-neurodivergent-wendys-employee-being-tied-kitchen-equipment/ "https://www.wsmv.com/2026/09/12/murfreesboro-police-reopen-investigation-into-neurodivergent-wendys-employee-being-tied-kitchen-equipment/")

In a recorded meeting with staff, an area manager called the incident “unacceptable” and said Burton was no longer a manager at the restaurant. The Wendy’s general manager also confirmed to WSMV4 Investigates that a manager was fired because of the incident.

WSMV4 Investigates attempted to contact Burton by phone and social media but did not receive a response.

In a statement, Wendy’s of Bowling Green, the franchisee that owns and operates the restaurant, said:

“The safety and well-being of our employees is our top priority. This behavior is inconsistent with our values and the standards we expect in our restaurants. Upon learning of the situation, it was promptly investigated and appropriate action was taken. We remain committed to maintaining a respectful workplace where all employees are treated with dignity and respect.”

# Restaurant says customer threatened to kill staff, including teen employee, over refund

Close

A Kansas City restaurant is warning against violence after a customer threatened to kill staff, including a teen, over a refund. (SOURCE: KCTV)

By [Sarah Motter](https://www.wsmv.com/authors/sarah.motter/) and [Andrew McMunn](https://www.wsmv.com/authors/andrew-mcmunn/)

Published: Jan. 12, 2026 at 1:26 AM UTC

Share

[Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=https://www.wsmv.com)

KANSAS CITY, Mo. ([KCTV](https://www.kctv5.com/2026/01/10/kansas-city-restaurant-issues-warning-after-customer-threatened-kill-staff-including-teen/ "https://www.kctv5.com/2026/01/10/kansas-city-restaurant-issues-warning-after-customer-threatened-kill-staff-including-teen/")/Gray News) – A restaurant in Missouri is warning against violence after they said a customer threatened to kill its staff, including a teenager, over a refund.

[Paul’s Drive In](https://www.paulsdriveinkc.com/) posted on social media that the incident happened on Wednesday night, Jan. 7, at its Blue Ridge Blvd. location.

The restaurant’s management said the customer asked for a refund and became verbally aggressive. The situation then escalated to explicit death threats against multiple workers.

“Last night, our team experienced a situation that crossed a line no service worker should ever have to face,” the restaurant said in the post.

The restaurant said the refund was already being processed when the threats started. It said staff are trained to prioritize safety above all else.

“We want to be very clear: this is not about a refund or a disagreement over food. Those situations happen in the service industry, and we work hard to resolve them calmly and fairly every day,” Co-owner Amanda Fulbright said. “What crossed the line, and what makes this incident especially concerning, were threats of violence that escalated to death threats directed at our employees.”

The restaurant owners said the individual was removed from the property after the transaction was completed.

The restaurant said its security cameras recorded the entire encounter. However, it will not be released as Fulbright said the goal is not to shame the individual, but to protect staff members.

“Let us be absolutely clear: Threatening violence over a food order is not acceptable. Ever,” management said. “It is not ‘passion.’ It is not ‘frustration.’ It is assault under Missouri law.”

Management said the customer has been permanently banned from Paul’s Drive In.

“We go out of our way to take care of our customers, but we will not tolerate threats, intimidation or abuse of our staff, especially our minors,” the post said.

The restaurant said violence against service workers is rising and “it has to stop.”

“Zero tolerance means zero tolerance. Our staff - especially minors - deserve to feel safe at work,” the owners said. “Threats of violence will result in immediate removal, a permanent ban, and law enforcement involvement. If you can’t treat people with respect, Paul’s is not the place for you.”

Fulbright said law enforcement was contacted, and her team continues to work through the appropriate legal channels.

In the coming days, she noted that new in-store signage will be posted to clearly outline the restaurant’s commitment to the respectful treatment of both customers and employees.

According to Fulbright, the signage will also emphasize an important component: “We are proud to employ and protect young workers.”

Fulbright also said the restaurant has been overwhelmed by the support from community members and fellow service industry workers.

“Our hope in speaking out is not to sensationalize what happened, but to help de-normalize abusive behavior toward service workers and to make it clear that kindness and basic decency are the standard—at Paul’s and everywhere," Fulbright said.

# ‘Situation is unfortunate’: Multiple Applebee’s restaurants suddenly close overnight

Close

Multiple Applebee’s restaurants across the Kansas City metro area suddenly closed this week. (Source: KCTV)

By [Sarah Motter](https://www.wsmv.com/authors/sarah.motter/) and [Jordan Gartner](https://www.wsmv.com/authors/jordan-gartner/)

Published: Oct. 31, 2024 at 12:46 AM UTC

Share

[Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=https://www.wsmv.com)

KANSAS CITY, Mo. ([KCTV](https://www.kctv5.com/2024/10/30/multiple-applebees-locations-close-kansas-city-metro-overnight/)/Gray News) - Multiple Applebee’s restaurant locations across the Kansas City metro area have suddenly closed.

Many [Applebee’s](https://www.applebees.com/en/menu?utm_medium=cpc&utm_source=Google&utm_content=cpc&utm_campaign=Menu&&&&&gad_source=1&gclid=Cj0KCQjwsoe5BhDiARIsAOXVoUsSkDQ0EK7dQk9UKhOQk8JIipKst_ukXz8rJrLFEJsVs4nicnKdlMsaAmr1EALw_wcB&gclsrc=aw.ds)employees in Kansas City woke up Wednesday morning to the news of the sudden restaurant closings.

Company officials confirmed the closures and said the locations affected were independently owned.

“Applebee’s restaurants are independently owned and operated by franchisees. The closure of eight restaurants in the Kansas City market looks to be the result of financial circumstances and decisions made by the franchisee,” Applebee’s President Tony Moralejo said. “This situation is unfortunate, and we continue to believe the Kansas City area is a great neighborhood for Applebee’s restaurants.”

Moralejo continued, “Two Applebee’s restaurants continue to serve our guests in the Kansas City area.”

Company officials noted that while they typically do not discuss individual franchisees, this particular entity has had periods when they have not been in good standing with the brand and has proven to not represent the brand well in the Kansas City market.

The two Applebee’s restaurants that remain open in the area are the Blue Springs and Gladstone locations.

## Applebee’s Franchise Costs: Estimated Initial Investment (Item 7, 2021 FDD)

*   The following table shows the franchisor’s current estimates of the initial investment likely to be required for the development and opening of Applebee’s newest Restaurant prototype.

*   The low range of the costs in the table typically reflects the franchisor’s estimate of costs for a 169-seat version of the newest prototype.

*   The high range of the costs in the table typically reflects the franchisor’s estimate of costs for a 225-seat version of the newest prototype and also takes into account some add-ons that may increase the investment cost, including enhanced fire alarm systems, pylon signs, and costs relating to expanding the Restaurant to accommodate up to 275 seats.

*   The figures in the table reflect the franchisor’s estimate of your initial investment from the time you sign a Development Agreement through approximately 3 months after you open your first Restaurant.

*   The total estimated initial investment includes pro-rated costs and expenses related to on-line ordering, wi-fi services, digital products service fee, server tablet maintenance fee, gateway processing fee, Waitlist, campaign/menu training, and training for 3 months.

*   The estimates for construction costs are based on the most recent costs or on the expected costs for franchisees’ Restaurants to be opened in 2020.

**1. Initial Organizational and Training Expenses (incorporation, legal and accounting fees, training, site location, and miscellaneous expenses): $75,000 to $120,000**

**2. Purchase of Land: $300,000 to $2,000,000**

*   The cost to purchase land varies because of geographic location. If you do not purchase the land and building for the Restaurant, you will need to lease this property, in which case a security deposit may be required.

*   Typical annual rents, which vary widely depending on factors like size, location, and condition of the leased premises, may range from 4% to over 8% of the Restaurant’s Gross Sales per year.

*   Also, you might incur certain construction or remodeling costs for necessary leasehold improvements.

*   Free-standing Restaurant sizes using the newest prototype range from approximately 4,500 square feet (seating 168) to approximately 5,410 square feet (seating 225), and Restaurants located in strip centers, shopping centers, and malls generally require more square footage to achieve the same seating.

**3. Building Costs (purchase, construction, remodeling, etc.): $556,000 to $2,600,000**

**14. Franchise Fee Deposit: $0 to $10,000**

**15. Initial Franchise Fee: $35,000 (if Franchise Fee Deposit paid, then less $10,000, for a total of $25,000)**

*   When you sign the Development Agreement, you may be required to prepay a portion of the total franchise fees for the Restaurants the franchisor requires you to develop during the initial years of the Development Agreement.

*   This amount will vary based on your development obligations during the “initial development periods”. If required, the franchise fee deposit will equal $10,000 per Restaurant.

*   Application of a part of the franchise fee deposit reduces the franchise fee. The 2 installments are due as follows: 50% when you sign the Franchise Agreement and the remaining balance 14 days before you are scheduled to open the Restaurant.

**16. Initial Advertising Expense: $5,000 to $40,000**

*   You must conduct an advertising campaign to promote the opening of the Restaurant, and the franchisor will reimburse you for 50% of your expenditures for such advertising campaign up to a maximum of $2,500 if you comply with the requirements described in the Franchise Agreement and the Field Marketing Internet.

**17. Liquor License(s): $500 to $1,000,000**

*   The amount necessary to obtain a liquor license varies greatly depending on the city, county, and state licensing authority involved and may be based on whether a license is available from the licensing authority or must be purchased from a third party.

**18. Apple Supply Chain Co-Op Stock Purchase: $0 to $100**

*   Membership in the Apple Supply Chain Co-op, Inc. (“Apple Co-op”) is voluntary. If you choose to join, this fee must be paid. Payment must be made to Apple Co-op and not to the franchisor.

**19. On-Line Ordering: $56 to $150 per month**

*   You must sign an Authorized Operator Agreement with Mobo Systems, Inc. (or another vendor approved by Applebee’s) for access and use of an approved provider’s on-line ordering system in form and substance approved by Applebee’s. These figures include the estimated cost for services provided by Mobo Systems, Inc. and a payment gateway provider related to on-line ordering.

**20. Europay, Mastercard, and Visa (“EMV”) Point-to-Point Encryption (“P2P”) Services: $1,500 to $3,000**

*   You must purchase equipment and procure services from an approved payment gateway vendor for credit card processing services. These figures include the estimated cost to purchase the equipment and a monthly fee of $66 to $130.

**21. Wi-Fi Services: $90 to $400 per month**

*   You must have a secure Wi-Fi connection in your Restaurant with sufficient bandwidth to support Restaurant operations and guests’ needs. Wi-Fi connection is required in order to utilize Applebee’s University and other technology platforms, including server tablets.

**22. Wi-Fi Equipment: $300 to $600**

*   You must make a one-time purchase of commercial Wi-Fi hardware that is approved by the franchisor.

**23. Digital Products Service Fee: $150 to $350 per month**

*   Applebee’s currently requires “I’ve Arrived”, where applicable, and it may require other products from time to time in the future, including without limitation, guest payment and ordering from their own device (“Bring Your Own Device” or “Pay ‘N Go”).

*   The current fees reflect software as a service pricing but the franchisor may charge you transaction pricing in the future.

**24. Server Tablet Maintenance Fee: $0 to $1,000 per year**

*   There is an annual maintenance fee of $1,000 per Restaurant if server tablets are deployed (regardless of the number of tablets in the Restaurant).

*   Server tablets are currently optional but may be required in the future. If they are required in the future, they must be pre-approved by the franchisor.

**25. Implementation Fees: $240 to $450**

*   These fees relate to deployment and support for hardware and software upgrades, as well as other products.

**26. Menu Management Platform Fee: $0 to $150 per month**

*   This fee relates to providing menu management capabilities including integrations to other digital platforms and A1POS. This fee is currently optional but may be required in the future.

**27. Customer Relationship Management (“CRM”) Fee: $0 to $150 per month**

*   This fee may be funded by the Applebee’s National Advertising Fund or there could be all or a portion of the fees required to be paid directly by the franchisee.

**28. Gateway Processing Fee: $66 per month**

*   This fee covers transaction processing costs to route transactions from the POS to the credit or gift card provider. These fees are in addition to any processing fees charged by your credit card and gift card processors.

**29. Waitlist: $0 to $69 per month**

*   Waitlist enables restaurants to seat more guests, more efficiently through a service provided by NoWait or WaitWhile.

*   Waitlist is currently optional but may be required by Applebee’s in the future.

**30. ROSnet – Food Cost, Labor, and Business Analytics Reporting Service: $200 set up per location; $75 to $225 per month****(depending on modules selected)**

**31. Campaign/Menu Training: $30 per year**

*   This training is required.

**32. Training: Applebee’s University (or a future learning management system training program provided by the franchisor) or Your Selected Training Program Approved by the Franchisor: $120 per year**

*   This training is required.

**33. Extra Manuals: $0 to $250 per set**

*   Payable if you want extra manuals, training materials, and other similar documents. The franchisor makes the first set available to you for free.

**34. Operating Expenses During First Three Months: $405,000 to $655,000**

*   This estimates your initial operating expenses for 3 months of operation. These expenses include working capital, payroll costs, food and liquor costs, utilities, ordinary maintenance, local advertising, royalty fees, advertising fees, telecommunication services, Internet, and other expenses normal in operating a Restaurant.

**35. Total: $2,009,201 to $8,266,730**

*   The franchisor relied on its experience and the experience of its affiliates and franchisees who provided projected or actual costs of Restaurants to compile this estimate.

# Multiple Applebee’s locations close in the Kansas City metro

Close

Multiple Applebee’s locations across the Kansas City metro closed seemingly overnight as employees woke to find news of the closures in their inboxes.

By [Sarah Motter](https://www.kctv5.com/authors/sarah.motter/)

Published: Oct. 30, 2024 at 6:36 PM UTC

Share

[Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=https://www.kctv5.com)

KANSAS CITY, Mo. (KCTV) - Multiple Applebee’s locations across the Kansas City metro closed seemingly overnight as employees woke to find news of the closures in their inboxes.

As many [Applebee’s](https://www.applebees.com/en/menu?utm_medium=cpc&utm_source=Google&utm_content=cpc&utm_campaign=Menu&&&&&gad_source=1&gclid=Cj0KCQjwsoe5BhDiARIsAOXVoUsSkDQ0EK7dQk9UKhOQk8JIipKst_ukXz8rJrLFEJsVs4nicnKdlMsaAmr1EALw_wcB&gclsrc=aw.ds)employees across the metro awoke on Wednesday morning, Oct. 30, news they may need to find a new job started to fill their inboxes. However, the company said the closures were not sanctioned by the brand.

“Applebee’s restaurants are independently owned and operated by franchisees. The closure of eight restaurants in the Kansas City market look to be the result of financial circumstances and decisions made by the franchisee,” said Applebee’s President Tony Moralejo. “This situation is unfortunate, and we continue to believe the Kansas City area is a great neighborhood for Applebee’s restaurants. We are exploring options about the future of these restaurants. Two Applebee’s restaurants continue to serve our guests in the Kansas City area.”

Company officials noted that while they typically do not discuss individual franchisees, this particular entity has had periods of time when they have not been in good standing with the brand and has proven to not represent the brand well in the Kansas City market.

KCTV5 has called various Applebee’s locations in the metro area and has received responses from employees at the Blue Springs location, 1100 NW Highway 7, and the Gladstone location, 6069 NE Antioch Rd., that both remain open.

Asian food in its many different forms is increasingly popular in America, and has become the basis for several successful franchises.

## The Popularity of Asian Food

Asian restaurant chains don’t currently have the huge reach of those working in some other cuisines, such as burgers and pizza. The leading Asian chain in the US has a couple thousand outlets, compared with the likes of McDonald’s and Domino’s that can count their outlets in the tens of thousands. But while there aren’t many dominant chains, Asian cuisine is hugely popular, with thousands of restaurants across the US. A lack of consolidation means that there are opportunities for franchises.

Asian food is popular among people seeking diverse cuisine, especially in urban areas. This encourages a diverse range of restaurants, some of them mixing up styles from different countries while others go more specific, presenting food from specific regions. The industry is seeing changes, as a [new generation of chefs](https://www.msn.com/en-us/foodanddrink/foodnews/new-generation-of-asian-american-restaurant-owners-using-parents-ingredients-and-their-own-creativity-to-elevate-menus/ar-AA1sn58S) adapts the cuisine passed down to them by their parents, bringing in adaptations based on American dining or fresh ideas from back home, and this adds to the sense that this is the go-to cuisine for those seeking something new.

The growth of Asian food in America partly reflects a global phenomenon. Asian styles are [increasingly popular around the world](https://www.msn.com/en-in/foodanddrink/other/asian-cuisine-will-dominate-world-food-landscape/ar-AA1sDvKp), and Asian chefs are becoming more confident in focusing on their native cuisines rather than trying to cater to western tastes. This has led to a boom in new approaches as well as the revival of old ones, and innovations developed in this confident culinary atmosphere are being carried into the US.

The restaurant industry is a fiercely competitive one, so it’s worth considering the advantages of specific Asian cuisines, so that you can pick one that will suit your territory.

## Chinese Food

[39% of Asian American restaurants](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2023/05/23/71-of-asian-restaurants-in-the-u-s-serve-chinese-japanese-or-thai-food/) serve Chinese food, making it the most popular option. These restaurants present a varied and iconic menu that’s become comfortingly familiar for many Americans, with plenty of choice and options they understand. It’s the most visible face of Asian food.

As a result, the Chinese restaurant industry is big business, worth [$27 billion in 2024](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/market-research-reports/chinese-restaurants-industry/), with an [average growth rate of 4.7% per year since 2018](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/market-research-reports/chinese-restaurants-industry/). Healthy eating seems to be helping Chinese restaurants. They often provide food that’s quick, convenient, and familiar – what consumers look for in quick service restaurants – without the unhealthy image that’s become attached to foods such as burgers. Less salt and fat, as well as more visible vegetables, make this a health-conscious choice.

## Japanese Food

With powerful and popular flavors such as soy sauce, wasabi, and pickled ginger, Japanese cuisine has become immensely popular in recent decades, spreading alongside Japanese culture and technology. Revenues from Japanese restaurants have been rising over the past five years, to reach [$32.2 billion in 2024](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/market-research-reports/japanese-restaurants-industry/).

Japanese food has particularly benefited from its popularity among younger consumers, who enjoy both its variety and the colorful way in which it’s often presented. Sushi has long been the iconic Japanese dish, and makes up [three-quarters of the sales](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/market-research-reports/japanese-restaurants-industry/) from Japanese restaurants, but ramen, bento, and even Japanese steaks are also increasingly well-known and popular.

With [nearly 23,000 restaurants across the country](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/market-research-reports/japanese-restaurants-industry/), Japanese restaurants are relatively widespread. Uneven distribution means that there’s strong competition in some areas but less in others, so it’s worth looking to see where there are demographics that might want access to a bento box but don’t have it yet.

## Thai Food

The [third most popular cuisine](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2023/05/23/71-of-asian-restaurants-in-the-u-s-serve-chinese-japanese-or-thai-food/) on Asian American restaurant menus, after Chinese and Japanese, there are around [5,300 Thai restaurants](https://www.vice.com/en/article/the-surprising-reason-that-there-are-so-many-thai-restaurants-in-america/) across the US. This presence is disproportionately large compared with the Thai population and comes from a peculiarity of how this food spread.

The expansion of Thai cuisine around the world was accelerated by a [deliberate effort by the Thai government](https://www.vice.com/en/article/the-surprising-reason-that-there-are-so-many-thai-restaurants-in-america/) in the early 2000s, using food as a tool of soft diplomacy.
